refs.text: 一径到了冯紫英家门口，有人报与了冯紫英，出来迎接进去。只见薛蟠早已在那里久候，还有许多唱曲儿的小厮并唱小旦的蒋玉菡、锦香院的妓女云儿。大家都见过了，然后吃茶。宝玉擎茶笑道：“前儿所言幸与不幸之事，我昼悬夜想，今日一闻呼唤即至。”冯紫英笑道：“你们令表兄弟倒都心实。前日不过是我的设辞，诚心请你们一饮，恐又推托，故说下这句话。今日一邀即至，谁知都信真了。”说毕大家一笑，然后摆上酒来，依次坐定。

且说宝玉在楼上，坐在贾母旁边，因叫个小丫头子捧着方才那一盘子贺物，将自己的玉带上，用手翻弄寻拨，一件一件的挑与贾母看。贾母因看见有个赤金点翠的麒麟，便伸手拿了起来，笑道：“这件东西好像我看见谁家的孩子也带着这么一个的。”宝钗笑道：“史大妹妹有一个，比这个小些。”贾母道：“是云儿有这个。”宝玉道：“他这么往我们家去住着，我也没看见。”探春笑道：“宝姐姐有心，不管什么他都记得。”林黛玉冷笑道：“他在别的上还有限，惟有这些人带的东西上越发留心。”宝钗听说，便回头装没听见。宝玉听见史湘云有这件东西，自己便将那麒麟忙拿起来揣在怀里。

refs.text: 宝玉听了，笑道：“这是怎么个原故？怎么林姑娘的倒不同我的一样，倒是宝姐姐的同我一样！别是传错了罢？”袭人道：“昨儿拿出来，都是一份一份的写着签子，怎么就错了！你的是在老太太屋里的，我去拿了来了。老太太说了，明儿叫你一个五更天进去谢恩呢。”宝玉道：“自然要走一趟。”说着便叫紫绡来：“拿了这个到林姑娘那里去，就说是昨儿我得的，爱什么留下什么。”紫绡答应了，拿了去，不一时回来说：“林姑娘说了，昨儿也得了，二爷留着罢。”

袭人见他脸都气黄了，眼眉都变了，从来没气的这样，便拉着他的手，笑道：“你同妹妹拌嘴，不犯着砸他，倘或砸坏了，叫他心里脸上怎么过的去？”林黛玉一行哭着，一行听了这话说到自己心坎儿上来，可见宝玉连袭人不如，越发伤心大哭起来。心里一烦恼，方才吃的香薷饮解暑汤便承受不住，“哇”的一声都吐了出来。紫鹃忙上来用手帕子接住，登时一口一口的把一块手帕子吐湿。雪雁忙上来捶。紫鹃道：“虽然生气，姑娘到底也该保重着些。才吃了药好些，这会子因和宝二爷拌嘴，又吐出来。倘或犯了病，宝二爷怎么过的去呢？”宝玉听了这话说到自己心坎儿上来，可见黛玉不如一紫鹃。

It was about the second watch that night before Feng Su came home, delighted with himself. Everyone pressed him to explain.
‘Our newly appointed prefect is a man named Jia Hua, originally from Huzhou. He used to be a friend of my son-in-law. He passed our door just now and saw that maid Jiao-xing buying thread, so he supposed my son-in-law had moved in here. I explained everything. His Honour was quite distressed and sighed over it. earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 原来这林如海之祖，曾袭过列侯，今到如海，业经五世。起初时，只封袭三世，因当今隆恩盛德，远迈前代，额外加恩，至如海之父，又袭了一代；至如海，便从科第出身。虽系钟鼎之家，却亦是书香之族。只可惜这林家支庶不盛，子孙有限，虽有几门，却与如海俱是堂族而已，没甚亲支嫡派的。今如海年已四十，只有一个三岁之子，偏又于去岁死了。虽有几房姬妾，奈他命中无子，亦无可如何之事。今只有嫡妻贾氏，生得一女，乳名黛玉，年方五岁。夫妻无子，故爱如珍宝，且又见他聪明清秀，便也欲使他读书识得几个字，不过假充养子之意，聊解膝下荒凉之叹。
earlier_text_evidence.english: An ancestor of Lin Ru-hai had held a hereditary marquisate; Ru-hai was now the fifth generation. Originally the title had been granted for three generations only. But the munificence and virtue of the present sovereign so far surpassed those of earlier reigns that an additional favour had allowed Ru-hai’s father to inherit it for a fourth generation. Ru-hai himself had entered official life through the examinations. His family belonged to the hereditary nobility, with its bells and bronze vessels, but it also had a tradition of learning. Unfortunately, the Lin clan had few branches and few descendants. There were several households, but these were only collateral relations of Ru-hai’s, with no close kin in his direct line. He was now forty. His only son, a boy of three, had died the previous year. He had several concubines, but no son was allotted to him by fate, and nothing could be done about it. His lawful wife, a lady of the Jia family, had borne him a daughter, known from infancy as Dai-yu, who was just five. Having no son, husband and wife treasured her. She was bright and delicate-looking, too, and they wished her to study and learn a few characters, merely to stand in, as it were, for the son they were not raising, and ease their sorrow at the emptiness about their knees.

earlier_text_evidence.english: ‘“To recover, she must never again be exposed to the sound of weeping. Apart from her parents, she must see no relations or friends of another surname. Only then can she live out her life in peace.” He was quite mad, talking such nonsense, and nobody paid him any attention. I am still taking ginseng pills to nourish the blood.’

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 说话时，已摆了茶果上来，熙凤亲为捧茶捧果。又见二舅母问他：“月钱放过了不曾？”熙凤道：“月钱已放完了。才刚带着人到后楼上找缎子，找了这半日，也并没有见昨日太太说的那样的。想是太太记错了？”王夫人道：“有没有，什么要紧。”因又说道：“该随手拿出两个来给你这妹妹去裁衣裳的，等晚上想着叫人再去拿罢，可别忘了。”熙凤道：“这倒是我先料着了，知道妹妹不过这两日到的，我已预备下了，等太太回去过了目好送来。”王夫人一笑，点头不语。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
While they were talking, tea and fruit had been laid out. Xi-feng herself presented Dai-yu with both. Dai-yu then heard her second aunt ask Xi-feng, ‘Have the monthly allowances been paid?’
‘They’ve all been paid. I was just taking some people up to the back storey to look for satin. We hunted for ages and couldn’t find the kind you mentioned yesterday. Perhaps you remembered it wrongly, ma’am?’
‘It hardly matters whether there is any,’ Lady Wang said. Then she added, ‘You should have taken out a couple of lengths while you were there, to make clothes for your cousin. Remind me this evening to have someone fetch them. Don’t forget.’
‘I had thought of that already,’ said Xi-feng. ‘Knowing she was due any day now, I’ve set some aside. Once you’ve been back and seen them, I can send them over.’
Lady Wang smiled and nodded without speaking.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 当下茶果已撤，贾母命两个老嬷嬷带了黛玉去见两个母舅。时贾赦之妻邢氏忙亦起身，笑回道：“我带了外甥女过去，倒也便宜。”贾母笑道：“正是呢，你也去罢，不必过来了。”邢夫人答应了一声“是”字，遂带了黛玉与王夫人作辞，大家送至穿堂前。出了垂花门，早有众小厮们拉过一辆翠幄青紬车。邢夫人携了黛玉，坐在上面，众婆子们放下车帘，方命小厮们抬起，拉至宽处，方驾上驯骡，亦出了西角门，往东过荣府正门，便入一黑油大门中，至仪门前方下来。众小厮退出，方打起车帘，邢夫人搀着黛玉的手，进入院中。黛玉度其房屋院宇，必是荣府中花园隔断过来的。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
When the tea and fruit had been cleared away, Grandmother Jia told two old nurses to take Dai-yu to pay her respects to her two maternal uncles. Jia She’s wife, Lady Xing, rose too.
‘It would be convenient for me to take my niece over,’ she said with a smile.
‘Yes, do go,’ Grandmother Jia replied, smiling. ‘You needn’t come back here.’
Lady Xing answered, ‘Yes,’ and took Dai-yu to say goodbye to Lady Wang. Everyone accompanied them as far as the passage-hall. Outside the flower-carved gate the young servants had already brought up a carriage with green curtains and a blue silk cover. Lady Xing took Dai-yu inside. The women lowered the curtains before ordering the young servants to lift and draw it to a wider space, where a docile mule was harnessed to it. They too went out through the small western gate, turned east past the main entrance of the Rong mansion and entered a great black-lacquered gateway, stopping before the ceremonial inner gate. Only after the young servants had withdrawn were the carriage curtains raised. Holding Dai-yu by the hand, Lady Xing led her into the courtyard. From the arrangement of the buildings and courtyards, Dai-yu judged that this must have been partitioned off from the Rong mansion’s garden.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 黛玉一一的都答应着。只见一个丫鬟来回：“老太太那里传晚饭了。”王夫人忙携黛玉从后房门由后廊往西，出了角门，是一条南北宽夹道。南边是倒座三间小小的抱厦厅，北边立着一个粉油大影壁，后有一半大门，小小一所房室。王夫人笑指向黛玉道：“这是你凤姐姐的屋子，回来你好往这里找他来，少什么东西，你只管和他说就是了。”这院门上也有四五个才总角的小厮，都垂手侍立。王夫人遂携黛玉穿过一个东西穿堂，便是贾母的后院了。于是，进入后房门，已有多人在此伺候，见王夫人来了，方安设桌椅。贾珠之妻李氏捧饭，熙凤安箸，王夫人进羹。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Dai-yu agreed to each of these instructions. A maid then came to announce, ‘Supper is being served at Her Old Ladyship’s.’
Lady Wang at once took Dai-yu through the rear doorway, west along the covered walk and out through a side gate into a broad north–south passage between walls. To the south stood a small three-bay hall, its back towards the outer approach, with a projecting covered porch; to the north was a great screen wall painted white. Behind it were a smallish gateway and a small set of rooms.
Lady Wang pointed them out with a smile. ‘Those are your Cousin Feng’s rooms. You can come and find her here later. Whatever you need, just tell her.’
Four or five young servants, still with their hair tied in little children’s tufts, stood by the courtyard gate with their hands at their sides. Lady Wang led Dai-yu through another east–west passage-hall into Grandmother Jia’s rear courtyard. They entered by the back door, where many attendants were already waiting. Only when Lady Wang arrived were the table and chairs set in place. Jia Zhu’s wife, née Li, brought the rice; Xi-feng laid out the chopsticks; Lady Wang presented the soup.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾母正面榻上独坐，两边四张空椅，熙凤忙拉了黛玉在左边第一张椅上坐了，黛玉十分推让。贾母笑道：“你舅母你嫂子们不在这里吃饭。你是客，原应如此坐的。”黛玉方告了座，坐了。贾母命王夫人坐了。迎春姊妹三个告了座方上来。迎春便坐右手第一，探春左第二，惜春右第二。旁边丫鬟执着拂尘、漱盂、巾帕。李、凤二人立于案旁布让。外间伺候之媳妇丫鬟虽多，却连一声咳嗽不闻。寂然饭毕，各有丫鬟用小茶盘捧上茶来。当日林如海教女以惜福养身，云饭后务待饭粒咽尽，过一时再吃茶，方不伤脾胃。今黛玉见了这里许多事情不合家中之式，不得不随的，少不得一一改过来，因而接了茶。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Grandmother Jia sat alone on the couch facing the room, with four empty chairs, two on either side. Xi-feng hurried to draw Dai-yu to the first chair on the left, but Dai-yu was most reluctant to accept it.
‘Your aunts and your cousins’ wives don’t eat here,’ Grandmother Jia said, smiling. ‘You are our guest. That is where you ought to sit.’
Only then did Dai-yu ask leave to be seated and sit down. Grandmother Jia told Lady Wang to sit. Ying-chun and the other two girls likewise asked leave before coming forward. Ying-chun took the first chair on the right, Tan-chun the second on the left, and Xi-chun the second on the right. Maids stood beside them holding fly-whisks, rinsing bowls and towels. Li and Xi-feng stood by the table, serving and inviting them to eat. Though many women servants and maids waited in the outer room, not so much as a cough was heard. The meal ended in silence. Maids brought each of them tea on small trays. Lin Ru-hai had taught his daughter to cherish her good fortune and preserve her health: after a meal she must be sure that every grain of rice had been swallowed and wait a while before drinking tea, so as not to harm the digestion. But Dai-yu had already seen many things here that differed from the customs at home and that she would have to follow. She must change her ways one by one. Accordingly she accepted the tea.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 黛玉道：“只刚念了《四书》。”黛玉又问姊妹们读何书。贾母道：“读的是什么书，不过是认得两个字，不是睁眼的瞎子罢了！”
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘I have only just been studying the Four Books,’ Dai-yu said. She then asked what her cousins were reading.
‘Reading?’ said Grandmother Jia. ‘They only learn a few characters, so that they won’t be blind with their eyes open!’

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 宝玉笑道：“我送妹妹一妙字，莫若‘颦颦’二字极妙。”探春便问何出。宝玉道：“《古今人物通考》上说：‘西方有石名黛，可代画眉之墨。’况这林妹妹眉尖若蹙，用取这两个字，岂不两妙！”探春笑道：“只恐又是你的杜撰。”宝玉笑道：“除《四书》外，杜撰的太多，偏只我是杜撰不成？”又问黛玉：“可也有玉没有？”
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘Let me give you a wonderful one,’ Bao-yu said, smiling. ‘Nothing could be better than Pin-pin, “Frown-frown”.’
Tan-chun asked where he had found it.
‘The Comprehensive Survey of Persons Past and Present says, “In the west is a stone called dai, which can be used instead of ink for painting eyebrows.” And Cousin Lin’s brows look as though they are drawn together in a frown. Don’t those two characters make it doubly apt?’
‘I’m afraid you’ve made that up again,’ Tan-chun said, laughing.
Bao-yu laughed too. ‘Apart from the Four Books, there’s plenty that’s made up. Why am I the only one accused of inventing things?’
He asked Dai-yu another question. ‘Have you a jade too?’

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 黛玉只带了两个人来：一个是自幼奶娘王嬷嬷，一个是十岁的小丫头，亦是自幼随身的，名唤作雪雁。贾母见雪雁甚小，一团孩气，王嬷嬷又极老，料黛玉皆不遂心省力的，便将自己身边的一个二等丫头，名唤鹦哥者与了黛玉。外亦如迎春等例，每人除自幼乳母外，另有四个教引嬷嬷，除贴身掌管钗盥沐两个丫鬟外，另有五六个洒扫房屋来往使役的小丫鬟。当下，王嬷嬷与鹦哥陪侍黛玉在碧纱橱内。宝玉之乳母李嬷嬷，并大丫鬟名唤袭人者，陪侍在外面大床上。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Dai-yu had brought only two attendants: Nurse Wang, who had nursed her from infancy, and a little maid of ten named Snowgoose, who had also been with her since she was very small. Grandmother Jia saw that Snowgoose was still thoroughly childish and Nurse Wang extremely old, and thought neither would be able to spare Dai-yu trouble or serve her as she wished. She therefore gave her one of her own second-ranking maids, called Ying-ge. In other respects Dai-yu was provided for on the same terms as Ying-chun and the others. Besides the nurse who had suckled each girl, there were four matrons to guide her conduct; besides the two personal maids who looked after her hair ornaments, washing and bathing, there were five or six little maids to sweep the rooms and run errands. Nurse Wang and Ying-ge now attended Dai-yu inside the green gauze screen. Outside, by the large bed, were Bao-yu’s wet-nurse, Nurse Li, and his senior maid, Aroma.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 原来这袭人亦是贾母之婢，本名珍珠。贾母因溺爱宝玉，生恐宝玉之婢无竭力尽忠之人，素喜袭人心地纯良，克尽职任，遂与了宝玉。宝玉因知他本姓花，又曾见旧人诗句上有“花气袭人”之句，遂回明贾母，更名袭人。这袭人亦有些痴处：伏侍贾母时，心中眼中只有一个贾母，如今服侍宝玉，心中眼中又只有一个宝玉。只因宝玉性情乖僻，每每规谏宝玉，心中着实忧郁。是晚，宝玉李嬷嬷已睡了，他见里面黛玉和鹦哥犹未安息，他自卸了妆，悄悄进来，笑问：“姑娘怎么还不安息？”黛玉忙让：“姐姐请坐。”袭人在床沿上坐了。鹦哥笑道：“林姑娘正在这里伤心，自己淌眼抹泪的说：‘今儿才来，就惹出你家哥儿的狂病，倘或摔坏了那玉，岂不是因我之过！’因此便伤心，我好容易劝好了。”袭人道：“姑娘快休如此，将来只怕比这个更奇怪的笑话儿还有呢！
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Aroma too had originally been Grandmother Jia’s maid, and her name had been Pearl. Doting on Bao-yu, Grandmother Jia had feared that none of his maids would give herself wholly to his service. She had always liked Aroma for her simple, good heart and the thoroughness with which she performed her duties, and had therefore given her to him. Bao-yu knew that her surname was Hua, ‘flower’, and had seen the phrase ‘the flowers’ aroma steals upon one’ in an old poem. He reported his wish to Grandmother Jia and changed her name to Aroma. Aroma had a certain single-mindedness of her own: when she served Grandmother Jia, the old lady alone filled her heart and eyes; now that she served Bao-yu, there was no one in her heart or eyes but Bao-yu. His perverse disposition, however, led her to remonstrate with him often and made her deeply anxious. That night, after Bao-yu and Nurse Li had gone to sleep, she saw that Dai-yu and Ying-ge were still awake inside. Having taken off her make-up, she slipped quietly in.
‘Why aren’t you resting yet, miss?’ she asked with a smile.
‘Please sit down, Sister,’ Dai-yu said at once.
Aroma sat on the edge of the bed.
‘Miss Lin has been upset,’ Ying-ge said, smiling. ‘She was crying and wiping her eyes, saying, “I had only just arrived, and already I brought on your young master’s madness. If he had broken the jade, wouldn’t it have been my fault?” That’s what was troubling her. I’ve only just managed to comfort her.’
‘Please don’t feel that way, miss,’ said Aroma. ‘You’ll probably see much stranger goings-on than that in future!

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 次日起来，省过贾母，因往王夫人处来，正值王夫人与熙凤在一处拆金陵来的书信看，又有王夫人之兄嫂处遣了两个媳妇来说话的。黛玉虽不知原委，探春等却都晓得是议论金陵城中所居的薛家姨母之子姨表兄薛蟠，倚财仗势，打死人命，现在应天府案下审理。如今母舅王子腾得了信息，故遣他家内的人来告诉这边，意欲唤取进京之意。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Next morning, after getting up and paying her respects to Grandmother Jia, Dai-yu went to Lady Wang’s apartments. Lady Wang and Xi-feng were together, opening letters from Jinling. Two married women servants had also been sent with a message from Lady Wang’s brother and his wife. Dai-yu knew nothing of the circumstances, but Tan-chun and the others knew that they were discussing Xue Pan, their maternal cousin, the son of Aunt Xue in Jinling. Relying on his wealth and influence, he had beaten a man to death, and the case was now before the Yingtian prefecture. Their uncle Wang Zi-teng had heard the news and sent members of his household to tell Lady Wang’s family, with the intention of having the Xues called to the capital.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 第三回 金陵城起复贾雨村 荣国府收养林黛玉

原来这李氏即贾珠之妻。珠虽夭亡，幸存一子，取名贾兰，今方五岁，已入学攻书。这李氏亦系金陵名宦之女，父名李守中，曾为国子监祭酒，族中男女无有不诵诗读书者。至李守中继承以来，便说“女子无才便有德”，故生了李氏时，便不十分令其读书，只不过将些《女四书》、《列女传》、《贤媛集》等三四种书，使他认得几个字，记得前朝这几个贤女便罢了，却只以纺绩井臼为要，因取名为李纨，字宫裁。因此这李纨虽青春丧偶，居家处膏粱锦绣之中，竟如槁木死灰一般，一概无见无闻，唯知侍亲养子，外则陪侍小姑等针黹诵读而已。今黛玉虽客寄于斯，日有这般姐妹相伴，除老父外，余者也都无庸虑及了。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
This Mrs Li was Jia Zhu’s wife. Though Zhu had died young, he had fortunately left a son, Jia Lan, now just five years old and already attending school. Mrs Li too came from a distinguished official family of Jinling. Her father, Li Shou-zhong, had been Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, and there was not a man or woman in the clan who did not study books and recite poetry. Once Li Shou-zhong became head of the family, however, he maintained that ‘A woman’s virtue lies in having no accomplishments.’ When his daughter was born, therefore, he did not have her taught very much. Three or four works, such as the Four Books for Women, the Lives of Exemplary Women and the Collected Lives of Worthy Ladies, would suffice: she need only learn to recognise a few characters and remember a few virtuous women of earlier dynasties. Spinning and weaving, drawing water and pounding grain were what mattered. Accordingly, he named her Li Wan and gave her the courtesy name Gong-cai.
Thus Li Wan, though widowed in the bloom of youth and living amid fine food and silks, was like dead wood and cold ashes. She took notice of nothing, heard nothing, and knew only the service of her elders and the upbringing of her son. Beyond these duties, she kept her young sisters-in-law company at their needlework and reading. Though Dai-yu was a guest beneath another’s roof, she now had these girls with her every day. Apart from her elderly father, there was nothing more she need trouble about.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 这薛家纵比冯家富贵，想其为人，自然姬妾众多，淫佚无度，未必及冯渊定情于一人者。这正是梦幻情缘，恰遇一对薄命儿女。且不要议论他，只目今这官司，如何剖断才好？”门子笑道：“老爷当年何其明决，今日何反成了个没主意的人了！小的闻得老爷补升此任，亦系贾府王府之力，此薛蟠即贾府之亲，老爷何不顺水行舟，作个整人情，将此案了结，日后也好去见贾府王府。”雨村道：“你说的何尝不是。但事关人命，蒙皇上隆恩，起复委用，实是重生再造，正当殚心竭力图报之时，岂可因私而废法？是我实不能忍为者。”门子听了，冷笑道：“老爷说的何尝不是大道理，但只是如今世上是行不去的。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘The Xues may be richer and grander than the Fengs, but, from the sort of man he is, I imagine he has any number of concubines and indulges himself without restraint. He may be very far from Feng Yuan, who gave his heart to one woman only. A bond of love as fleeting as a dream, and two ill-fated young people brought together! But let us leave them. What I need to know is how best to decide this case.’
The usher smiled. ‘Your Honour used to be so clear-headed and decisive. How is it that you cannot make up your mind today? I hear it was through the Jia and Wang families that you obtained this new appointment. Xue Pan is a relative of the Jias. Why not go with the current, do them a thorough good turn and settle the case? Then you will have something to say when you next call on the Jias and the Wangs.’
‘There is much in what you say,’ Yu-cun replied. ‘But a man’s life is involved. His Majesty’s great kindness in reinstating me and entrusting me with office has given me a second life. This is the very time when I ought to devote every effort to repaying him. How can I set the law aside for private interests? I truly could not bring myself to do it.’
The usher gave a cold laugh. ‘Your Honour’s principles are excellent. Only they will not work in the world as it is today.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 寡母王氏乃现任京营节度使王子腾之妹，与荣国府贾政的夫人王氏，是一母所生的姊妹，今年方四十上下年纪，只有薛蟠一子。还有一女，比薛蟠小两岁，乳名宝钗，生得肌骨莹润，举止娴雅。当日有他父亲在日，酷爱此女，令其读书识字，较之乃兄竟高过十倍。自父亲死后，见哥哥不能依贴母怀，他便不以书字为事，只留心针黹家计等事，好为母亲分忧解劳。近因今上崇诗尚礼，征采才能，降不世出之隆恩，除聘选妃嫔外，凡仕宦名家之女，皆亲名达部，以备选为公主、郡主入学陪侍，充为才人、赞善之职。二则自薛蟠父亲死后，各省中所有的买卖承局，总管、伙计人等，见薛蟠年轻不谙世事，便趁时拐骗起来，京都中几处生意，渐亦消耗。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
His widowed mother, née Wang, was a younger sister of Wang Zi-teng, the present Commander of the Metropolitan Garrison, and a sister by the same mother of Lady Wang, Jia Zheng’s wife at the Rong mansion. She was only about forty, and Xue Pan was her only son. She also had a daughter, two years younger than Xue Pan, whose childhood name was Bao-chai. The girl’s skin had a smooth, lustrous bloom, and her manner was composed and graceful. Her father had adored her and had her taught to read, and she was ten times the scholar her brother was. After her father’s death, seeing that her brother could do little to comfort their mother, she gave up making books her chief concern and turned instead to needlework and household affairs, hoping to ease her mother’s worries and spare her some labour.
Now the present sovereign, who honoured poetry and ritual and sought out talent, had recently bestowed an extraordinary favour. In addition to the selection of imperial consorts, the names of daughters from distinguished official families were all to be submitted to the appropriate board, so that some might be chosen as study companions for princesses of the imperial and princely houses, with appointments as Ladies of Talent and Ladies of Instruction. There was another consideration too. Since Xue Pan’s father had died, the managers and clerks of the family’s businesses and supply agencies in the provinces, seeing how young and inexperienced Xue Pan was, had seized the opportunity to cheat him. Several of the businesses in the capital were dwindling away as well.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 那时王夫人已知薛蟠官司一事，亏贾雨村维持了结，才放了心。又见哥哥升了边缺，正愁又少了娘家的亲戚来往，略加寂寞。过了几日，忽家人传报：“姨太太带了哥儿姐儿，合家进京，正在门外下车。”喜的王夫人忙带了女媳人等，接出大厅，将薛姨妈等接了进去。姊妹们暮年相会，自不必说悲喜交集，泣笑叙阔一番。忙又引了拜见贾母，将人情土物各种酬献了，合家俱厮见过，忙又治席接风。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Lady Wang had already heard how Jia Yu-cun had intervened to settle Xue Pan’s case, and her mind was now at ease. Then came the news of her brother’s promotion to a frontier post. She was feeling rather lonely at the thought that there would be one fewer member of her own family to see. A few days later a servant suddenly announced, ‘Your sister has brought the young master and young lady to the capital. The whole family is outside, getting out of the carriages.’
Delighted, Lady Wang hurried out to the main hall with the girls and daughters-in-law to welcome Aunt Xue and bring them in. The sisters were meeting again in their later years: there is no need to describe their mingled grief and joy, their tears and laughter as they spoke of their long separation. Lady Wang hastened to take them to pay their respects to Grandmother Jia, and the various presents and local specialities were offered. When everyone in the household had greeted them, a welcoming feast was quickly prepared.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 薛蟠已拜见过贾政，贾琏又引着拜见了贾赦，贾珍等。贾政便使人上来对王夫人说：“姨太太已有了春秋，外甥年轻不知世路，在外住着恐有人生事。咱们东北角上梨香院一所十来间房，白空闲着，打扫了，请姨太太和姐儿哥儿住了甚好。”王夫人未及留，贾母也就遣人来说“请姨太太就在这里住下，大家亲密些”等语。薛姨妈正要同居一处，方可拘紧些儿子，若另住在外，又恐他纵性惹祸，遂忙道谢应允。又私与王夫人说明：“一应日费供给一概免却，方是处常之法。”王夫人知他家不难于此，遂亦从其愿。从此后，薛家母子就在梨香院住了。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Xue Pan had already paid his respects to Jia Zheng, and Jia Lian took him to see Jia She, Jia Zhen and the others. Jia Zheng sent a message in to Lady Wang:
‘Your sister is getting on in years, and our nephew is young and knows nothing of the world. If they live outside, I fear someone may make trouble for them. There are a dozen rooms standing empty in Pear-tree Court, in the north-east corner of our grounds. It would be an excellent arrangement to have them cleaned and invite your sister and the two young people to stay there.’
Before Lady Wang could urge them to stay, Grandmother Jia too sent to say, ‘Ask your sister to make her home here, so that we can all be closer.’
Aunt Xue had wanted just such an arrangement, which would allow her to keep a tighter hold on her son. If they lived separately, she feared he would give his temper free rein and get into trouble again. She therefore thanked them warmly and accepted. In private, however, she made one point clear to Lady Wang:
‘You must leave all our daily expenses and provisions to us. That is the only way we can go on comfortably together.’
Lady Wang knew that her sister’s family could well afford them, and agreed. From then on Aunt Xue and her children lived in Pear-tree Court.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 原来这梨香院即当日荣公暮年养静之所，小小巧巧，约有十余间房屋，前厅后舍俱全。另有一门通街，薛蟠家人就走此门出入。西南有一角门，通一夹道，出夹道便是王夫人正房的东边了。每日或饭后，或晚间，薛姨妈便过来，或与贾母闲谈，或与王夫人相叙。宝钗日与黛玉迎春姊妹等一处，或看书下棋，或作针黹，倒也十分乐业。只是薛蟠起初之心，原不欲在贾宅居住者，但恐姨父管约拘禁，料必不自在的，无奈母亲执意在此，且宅中又十分殷勤苦留，只得暂且住下，一面使人打扫出自己的房屋，再移居过去的。谁知自从在此住了不上一月的光景，贾宅族中凡有的子侄，俱已认熟了一半，凡是那些纨绔气习者，莫不喜与他来往，今日会酒，明日观花，甚至聚赌嫖娼，渐渐无所不至，引诱的薛蟠比当日更坏了十倍。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Pear-tree Court had been the old Duke of Rong’s retreat in his later years. It was a neat little place of a dozen rooms or so, complete with a hall at the front and living quarters behind. A separate gate opened on to the street, and the Xue servants used it to come and go. In the south-west corner a side gate led into a narrow passage, which emerged on the east side of Lady Wang’s principal rooms. Every day, either after a meal or in the evening, Aunt Xue would come over to chat with Grandmother Jia or spend time with Lady Wang. Bao-chai passed her days with Dai-yu, Ying-chun and the other girls, reading, playing chess or doing needlework, and was very happy.
Xue Pan had originally been unwilling to live in the Jia household, fearing that his uncle would keep him in order and give him no freedom. But his mother was determined to stay, and the family pressed them so warmly that he had to remain for the time being. Meanwhile, he sent men to prepare one of his own houses, intending to move there later. Yet before he had been there a month he had become well acquainted with half the sons and nephews of the Jia clan. Every one of its idle young rakes was delighted to make his acquaintance. There was a drinking party today, an outing to see the flowers tomorrow; then came gambling parties and visits to prostitutes, until by degrees there was nothing they would not do. Under their influence Xue Pan grew ten times worse than before.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 自悔言语冒撞，前去俯就，那黛玉方渐渐的回转来。因东边宁府中花园内梅花盛开，贾珍之妻尤氏乃治酒，请贾母、邢夫人、王夫人等赏花。是日先携了贾蓉之妻，二人来面请。贾母等于早饭后过来，就在会芳园游顽，先茶后酒，不过皆是宁荣二府女眷家宴小集，并无别样新文趣事可记。一时宝玉倦怠，欲睡中觉，贾母命人好生哄着，歇一回再来。贾蓉之妻秦氏便忙笑回道：“我们这里有给宝叔收拾下的屋子，老祖宗放心，只管交与我就是了。”又向宝玉的奶娘丫鬟等道：“嬷嬷姐姐们，请宝叔随我这里来。”贾母素知秦氏是个极妥当的人，生的袅娜纤巧，行事又温柔和平，乃重孙媳中第一个得意之人，见他去安置宝玉，自是安稳的。
earlier_text_evidence.english: regretting his own rash words, went to make peace with her. Only then did she gradually relent. The plum blossom was now at its height in the garden of the Ning mansion to the east, and Jia Zhen’s wife, You-shi, arranged a party for Grandmother Jia, Lady Xing, Lady Wang and the others to enjoy it. That day she brought Jia Rong’s wife with her to deliver the invitation in person. Grandmother Jia and her party went over after breakfast and amused themselves in the Garden of Gathered Fragrance, taking tea first and wine afterwards. It was merely a small family gathering of the women from the Ning and Rong households; there were no other novelties or amusing incidents to record. Presently Bao-yu grew tired and wanted his midday nap. Grandmother Jia told his attendants to coax him gently to sleep and bring him back when he had rested. Jia Rong’s wife, Qin-shi, promptly answered with a smile, ‘We have a room all ready for Uncle Bao. Don’t worry, Great-grandmother. Just leave him to me.’ Then she turned to his nurse and maids. ‘Mamma, sisters, please bring Uncle Bao this way with me.’ Grandmother Jia had always known Qin-shi to be thoroughly capable. Delicate and graceful in appearance, gentle and even-tempered in her dealings, she was the old lady’s favourite among her great-grandsons’ wives. With Qin-shi seeing to Bao-yu, she naturally felt quite at ease.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 案上设着武则天当日镜室中设的宝镜，一边摆着飞燕立着舞过的金盘，盘内盛着安禄山掷过伤了太真乳的木瓜。上面设着寿昌公主于含章殿下卧的榻，悬的是同昌公主制的联珠帐。宝玉含笑连说：“这里好！”秦氏笑道：“我这屋子大约神仙也可以住得了。”说着亲自展开了西子浣过的纱衾，移了红娘抱过的鸳枕，于是众奶母伏侍宝玉卧好，款款散了，只留袭人、媚人、晴雯、麝月四个丫鬟为伴。秦氏便分咐小丫鬟们，好生在廊檐下看着猫儿狗儿打架。
earlier_text_evidence.english: On the table stood the precious mirror that had once furnished Wu Ze-tian’s mirror chamber. To one side was the golden platter on which Flying Swallow had danced; in it lay the quince An Lu-shan had thrown, bruising Tai-zhen’s breast. Further in stood the couch on which Princess Shou-chang had slept below the Hanzhang Hall, hung with the strung-pearl curtains Princess Tong-chang had had made. ‘This is lovely!’ Bao-yu said again and again, smiling. ‘I dare say even an immortal could live in this room of mine,’ Qin-shi said with a laugh. With her own hands she spread a gauze coverlet washed by Xi Shi and moved into place a lovers’ pillow once held by Hong-niang. The nurses settled Bao-yu in bed and gradually withdrew, leaving only the four maids Aroma, Winsome, Skybright and Musk to keep him company. Qin-shi told the little maids to keep a good watch under the eaves in case the cats and dogs started fighting.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 镜里恩情，更那堪梦里功名！那美韶华去之何迅！再休提锈帐鸳衾。只这带珠冠，披凤袄，也抵不了无常性命。虽说是，人生莫受老来贫，也须要阴骘积儿孙。气昂昂头戴簪缨；光灿灿腰悬金印；威赫赫爵禄高登，昏惨惨黄泉路近。问古来将相可还存？也只是虚名儿与后人钦敬。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Affection in a mirror,
and worse, distinction in a dream!
How swiftly lovely youth is gone.
Speak no more of embroidered curtains and lovers’ quilts.
Even wearing a pearl coronet
and a phoenix-patterned robe
cannot offset the impermanence of life.
Though they say none should suffer poverty in old age,
there is still a need to store hidden merit for one’s descendants.
Head held high beneath an official’s hat and tassels;
a golden seal hanging bright at the waist;
rank and stipend mounting in imposing splendour:
then darkness, and the road to the Yellow Springs draws near.
Where are the generals and ministers of old?
Only empty names remain for later people to admire.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 方才所说的这小小之家，乃本地人氏，姓王，祖上曾作过小小的一个京官，昔年与凤姐之祖王夫人之父认识。因贪王家的势利，便连了宗认作侄儿。那时只有王夫人之大兄凤姐之父与王夫人随在京中的，知有此一门连宗之族，余者皆不认识。目今其祖已故，只有一个儿子，名唤王成，因家业萧条，仍搬出城外原乡中住去了。王成新近亦因病故，只有其子，小名狗儿。狗儿亦生一子，小名板儿，嫡妻刘氏，又生一女，名唤青儿。一家四口，仍以务农为业，因狗儿白日间又作些生计，刘氏又操井臼等事，青板姊妹两个无人看管，狗儿遂将岳母刘姥姥接来一处过活。这刘姥姥乃是个积年的老寡妇，膝下又无儿女，只靠两亩薄田度日。
earlier_text_evidence.english: The little household just mentioned belonged to the Wang family, natives of the district. An ancestor had held a very minor post in the capital and had known Lady Wang’s father, Xi-feng’s grandfather. Coveting the influence and advantages of that family, he had claimed kinship through their shared surname and acknowledged himself a nephew. At the time, only Lady Wang and her eldest brother, Xi-feng’s father, had been living in the capital, so they alone knew of this branch of nominal relations; the others knew nothing of it. That ancestor was now dead. His only son, Wang Cheng, had seen the family fortunes decline and moved out of the city to their old village. Wang Cheng too had recently died of illness, leaving only his son, known by the childhood name Gou-er. Gou-er in turn had a son, called Ban-er, and his lawful wife, née Liu, had also borne him a daughter, Qing-er. This family of four still lived by farming. As Gou-er did other work during the day to earn a living, and his wife was busy drawing water, grinding grain and doing the housework, no one was left to look after the two siblings, Qing-er and Ban-er. Gou-er therefore brought his mother-in-law, Grannie Liu, to live with them. She was an old woman who had been widowed for many years, with no children at her side, subsisting on two mu of poor land.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 周瑞家的在内听说，忙迎了出来，问：“是那位？”刘姥姥忙迎上来问道：“好呀，周嫂子！”周瑞家的认了半日，方笑道：“刘姥姥，你好呀！你说说，能几年，我就忘了。请家里来坐罢。”刘姥姥一壁里走着，一壁笑说道：“你老是贵人多忘事，那里还记得我们呢。”说着，来至房中。周瑞家的命雇的小丫头倒上茶来吃着，周瑞家的又问板儿道：“你都长这们大了！”又问些别后闲话。又问刘姥姥：“今日还是路过，还是特来的？”刘姥姥便说：“原是特来瞧瞧嫂子你，二则也请请姑太太的安。若可以领我见一见更好，若不能，便借重嫂子转致意罢了。”周瑞家的听了，便已猜着几分来意。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Hearing this, Zhou Rui’s wife hurried out.
‘Who is it?’
Grannie Liu stepped forward. ‘How are you, Sister Zhou?’
Zhou Rui’s wife stared for a while before recognising her, then smiled.
‘Grannie Liu! How are you? Tell me, how many years has it been? I’ve quite forgotten. Come in and sit down.’
‘An important person like you has so much to remember,’ Grannie Liu said, smiling as she went in. ‘How could you remember us?’
Inside, Zhou Rui’s wife told a young maid she employed to pour tea.
‘How you’ve grown!’ she said to Ban-er.
After asking about various things that had happened since they last met, she turned to Grannie Liu.
‘Were you passing today, or have you come specially?’
‘I came specially to see you, Sister, and to pay my respects to Her Ladyship as well. If you could take me to see her, so much the better. If not, I’ll rely on you to pass on my respects.’
Zhou Rui’s wife had already guessed something of her purpose.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 刘姥姥听了，罕问道：“原来是他！怪道呢，我当日就说他不错呢。这等说来，我今儿还得见他了。”周瑞家的道：“这自然的。如今太太事多心烦，有客来了，略可推得去的就推过去了，都是凤姑娘周旋迎待。今儿宁可不会太太，倒要见他一面，才不枉这里来一遭。”刘姥姥道：“阿弥陀佛！全仗嫂子方便了。”周瑞家的道：“说那里话。俗语说的：‘与人方便，自己方便。’不过用我说一句话罢了，害着我什么。”说着，便叫小丫头到倒厅上悄悄的打听打听，老太太屋里摆了饭了没有。小丫头去了。这里二人又说些闲话。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘So it’s her!’ Grannie Liu exclaimed in surprise. ‘Well, no wonder. I said in those days she was a fine girl. Then I’ll get to see her today as well?’
‘Of course,’ said Zhou Rui’s wife. ‘Her Ladyship has so much to trouble her now that she passes on any visitor she can, and Miss Feng sees to them all. Even if you don’t see Her Ladyship today, you must see her, or your journey will have been wasted.’
‘Blessed Buddha! I’m entirely in your hands, Sister.’
‘Don’t say that. As the saying goes, “Make things easy for others and you make them easy for yourself.” It only costs me a word. What harm can it do me?’
She sent the young maid to the front hall to find out quietly whether the meal had been laid in Grandmother Jia’s rooms. The girl went off, and the two women talked of other things.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 先到了倒厅，周瑞家的将刘姥姥安插在那里略等一等。自己先过了影壁，进了院门，知凤姐未下来，先找着凤姐的一个心腹通房大丫头，名唤平儿的。周瑞家的先将刘姥姥起初来历说明，又说：“今日大远的特来请安。当日太太是常会的，今日不可不见，所以我带了他进来了。等奶奶下来，我细细回明，奶奶想也不责备我莽撞的。”平儿听了，便作了主意：“叫他们进来，先在这里坐着就是了。”
earlier_text_evidence.english:
At the front hall Zhou Rui’s wife settled Grannie Liu to wait a little, then went past the screen wall and through the courtyard gate herself. Finding that Xi-feng had not yet returned, she first sought out Patience, one of Xi-feng’s trusted senior chamber-maids, who also shared her master’s bed. Zhou Rui’s wife explained who Grannie Liu was and how she came to be there.
‘She’s come all this way today specially to pay her respects. Her Ladyship used to see her often, so we really couldn’t refuse to see her today. That’s why I’ve brought her in. When the mistress comes back, I’ll explain it all. I don’t think she’ll blame me for taking too much on myself.’
Patience made the decision.
‘Bring them in. They can sit here for the time being.’

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 周瑞家的听了，方出去引他两个进入院来。上了正房台矶，小丫头打起猩红毡帘，才入堂屋，只闻一阵香扑了脸来，竟不辨是何气味，身子如在云端里一般。满屋中之物都耀眼争光的，使人头悬目眩。刘姥姥此时惟点头咂嘴念佛而已。于是来至东边这间屋内，乃是贾琏的女儿大姐儿睡觉之所。平儿站在炕沿边，打量了刘姥姥两眼，只得问个好让坐。刘姥姥见平儿遍身绫罗，插金带银，花容玉貌的，便当是凤姐儿了。才要称姑奶奶，忽见周瑞家的称他是平姑娘，又见平儿赶着周瑞家的称周大娘，方知不过是个有些体面的丫头了。于是让刘姥姥和板儿上了炕，平儿和周瑞家的对面坐在炕沿上，小丫头子斟了茶来吃茶。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Only then did Zhou Rui’s wife go out and bring the two of them into the courtyard. They mounted the steps of the main rooms, and a young maid lifted a scarlet felt curtain. As soon as they entered the central room, a wave of fragrance struck Grannie Liu’s face. She could not tell what scent it was and felt as though she were floating among clouds. Everything in the room glittered and shone, dazzling her eyes and making her head swim. All she could do was nod, click her tongue and invoke the Buddha.
They went into the room on the east, where Jia Lian’s little daughter, Da-jie, slept. Patience stood by the edge of the kang, looked Grannie Liu over once or twice, then greeted her and offered her a seat. Seeing Patience dressed from head to foot in fine silks, wearing gold and silver, with a face as lovely as flowers and jade, Grannie Liu took her for Xi-feng. She was just about to address her as ‘Madam’ when she heard Zhou Rui’s wife call her ‘Miss Patience’, and Patience in turn address the other woman as ‘Mrs Zhou’. Only then did she realise that this was merely a maid of some standing. Grannie Liu and Ban-er were invited up on to the kang; Patience and Zhou Rui’s wife sat facing each other on its edge. A young maid poured tea for them.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 话说周瑞家的送了刘姥姥去后，便上来回王夫人话。谁知王夫人不在上房，问丫鬟们时，方知往薛姨妈那边闲话去了。周瑞家的听说，便转出东角门至东院，往梨香院来。刚至院门前，只见王夫人的丫鬟名金钏儿者，和一个才留了头的小女孩儿站在台阶坡上顽。见周瑞家的来了，便知有话回，因向内努嘴儿。周瑞家的轻轻掀帘进去，只见王夫人和薛姨妈长篇大套的说些家务人情等语。
earlier_text_evidence.english: After seeing Grannie Liu off, Zhou Rui’s wife went to report to Lady Wang. But Lady Wang was not in her principal rooms. On asking the maids, she learnt that Her Ladyship had gone to chat with Aunt Xue. She accordingly went out through the eastern side gate, crossed into the eastern courtyard and made her way to Pear-tree Court. Just outside its gate she saw Lady Wang’s maid Golden playing on the sloping approach to the steps with a little girl whose hair had only lately been allowed to grow. Seeing Zhou Rui’s wife, they knew she had something to report, and gestured towards the room with their lips. She lifted the curtain softly and went in. Lady Wang and Aunt Xue were deep in a long conversation about household affairs and their dealings with relatives and friends.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 周瑞家的不敢惊动，遂进里间来。只见薛宝钗穿着家常衣服，头上只散挽著纂儿，坐在炕边里，伏在小炕桌上同丫鬟莺儿正描花样子呢。见他进来，宝钗才放下笔，转过身来，满面堆笑让：“周姐姐坐。”周瑞家的也忙陪笑问：“姑娘好？”
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Not daring to interrupt, Zhou Rui’s wife went into the inner room. There sat Xue Bao-chai in her everyday clothes, her hair loosely coiled in a simple bun. She was sitting towards the inner end of the kang, leaning over its little table to trace embroidery patterns with her maid Oriole. At the sight of her visitor Bao-chai put down her brush and turned, her face all smiles. ‘Do sit down, Sister Zhou.’
Zhou Rui’s wife hastened to smile back. ‘Are you well, miss?’

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 如今从南带至北，现在就埋在梨花树底下呢。”周瑞家的又问道：“这药可有名子没有呢？”宝钗道：“有。这也是那癞头和尚说下的。叫作‘冷香丸’。”周瑞家的听了点头儿，因又说：“这病发了时到底觉怎么着？”宝钗道：“也不觉甚怎么着，只不过喘嗽些，吃一丸下去也就好些了。”周瑞家的还欲说话时，忽听王夫人问：“谁在房里呢？”周瑞家的忙出去答应了，趁便回了刘姥姥之事。略待半刻，见王夫人无语，方欲退出，薛姨妈忽又笑道：“你且站住。我有一宗东西，你带了去罢。”说着便叫香菱。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘We’ve brought it north from the south, and it’s buried under the pear tree at this very moment.’
‘Does the medicine have a name?’ Zhou Rui’s wife asked.
‘Yes. The scabby-headed monk gave us that too. They’re called “Cold Fragrance Pills”.’
Zhou Rui’s wife nodded. ‘And just how do you feel when the illness comes on?’
‘Nothing very much. I only get a little wheezy and cough. Once I’ve taken a pill, I feel rather better.’
Zhou Rui’s wife was about to speak again when she suddenly heard Lady Wang ask, ‘Who’s in there?’
She hurried out to answer, and took the opportunity to report about Grannie Liu. After waiting a little while and finding that Lady Wang had nothing more to say, she was just going to withdraw when Aunt Xue stopped her with a smile. ‘Wait a moment. I’ve something for you to take with you.’ She called for Caltrop.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 这日夜间，正和平儿灯下拥炉倦绣，早命浓薰绣被，二人睡下，屈指算行程该到何处，不知不觉已交三鼓。平儿已睡熟了。凤姐方觉星眼微蒙，恍惚只见秦氏从外走来，含笑说道：“婶婶好睡！我今日回去，你也不送我一程。因娘儿们素日相好，我舍不得婶子，故来别你一别。还有一件心愿未了，非告诉婶子，别人未必中用。”凤姐听了，恍惚问道：“有何心事？你只管托我就是了。”秦氏道：“婶婶，你是个脂粉队里的英雄，连那些束带顶冠的男子也不能过你，你如何连两句俗语也不晓得？常言‘月满则亏，水满则溢’；又道是‘登高必跌重’。如今我们家赫赫扬扬，已将百载，一日倘或乐极悲生，若应了那句‘树倒猢狲散’的俗语，岂不虚称了一世诗书旧族了！”凤姐听了此话，心胸大快，十分敬畏，忙问道：“这话虑的极是，但有何法可以永保无虞？”秦氏冷笑道：“婶子好痴也。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
One night the two of them sat by the brazier, tired of their embroidery beneath the lamp. Xi-feng had already ordered the embroidered quilts to be well warmed and scented. They lay down and counted off the days of the journey on their fingers, reckoning how far the travellers ought to have gone. Before she knew it, the third watch had begun. Patience was fast asleep. Xi-feng’s bright eyes were only just growing heavy when, dimly, she saw Qin-shi come in from outside. Smiling, she said, ‘How soundly you sleep, Aunt! I am going back today, and you have not even come to see me on my way. We have always been so close that I could not bear to leave you. That is why I have come to say goodbye. There is also one wish I have not fulfilled. I must tell you about it, Aunt. Someone else might be of no use.’
Still in a haze, Xi-feng asked, ‘What is troubling you? Whatever it is, leave it to me.’
‘Aunt,’ said Qin-shi, ‘you are a hero among women. Even the men in their caps and girdles cannot outdo you. How can you not know a couple of common sayings? “When the moon is full it begins to wane; when water is full it spills over.” And again, “The higher the climb, the harder the fall.” Our family has now enjoyed almost a hundred years of splendour. Suppose one day joy turned to sorrow, and the saying came true: “When the tree falls, the monkeys scatter.” Would all our claims to be an old family of learning not have been empty words?’
These words greatly heartened Xi-feng and filled her with awed respect. ‘You have thought this out very well,’ she said quickly. ‘But what can we do to keep ourselves safe for ever?’
Qin-shi gave a cold laugh. ‘How foolish you are, Aunt.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 然后又出来见贾珍。彼时贾代儒带领贾敕、贾效、贾敦、贾赦、贾政、贾琮、贾㻞、贾珩、贾珖、贾琛、贾琼、贾璘、贾蔷、贾菖、贾菱、贾芸、贾芹、贾蓁、贾萍、贾藻、贾蘅、贾芬、贾芳、贾兰、贾菌、贾芝等都来了。贾珍哭的泪人一般，正和贾代儒等说道：“合家大小，远亲近友，谁不知我这媳妇比儿子还强十倍。如今伸腿去了，可见这长房内绝灭无人了。”说着又哭起来。众人忙劝道：“人已辞世，哭也无益，且商议如何料理要紧。”
earlier_text_evidence.english:
He then came out to see Jia Zhen. Jia Dai-ru had arrived, bringing Jia Chi, Jia Xiao, Jia Dun, Jia She, Jia Zheng, Jia Cong, Jia Bin, Jia Heng, Jia Guang, Jia Chen, Jia Qiong, Jia Lin, Jia Qiang, Jia Chang, Jia Ling, Jia Yun, Jia Qin, Jia Zhen, Jia Ping, Jia Zao, Jia Heng, Jia Fen, Jia Fang, Jia Lan, Jia Jun and Jia Zhi. Jia Zhen was dissolved in tears. He was saying to Jia Dai-ru and the others, ‘Who among our household, old or young, our distant relations or our closest friends, did not know that this daughter-in-law of mine was ten times better than my son? Now she has stretched out her legs and gone. This senior branch of the family is finished. There is no one left.’ He began to weep again.
They hastened to comfort him. ‘She has passed away. Tears will do no good now. What matters is to decide how the arrangements are to be made.’

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾珍拍手道：“如何料理，不过尽我所有罢了！”正说着，只见秦业、秦钟并尤氏的几个眷属尤氏姊妹也都来了。贾珍便命贾琼、贾琛、贾璘、贾蔷四个人去陪客，一面吩咐去请钦天监阴阳司来择日，推准停灵七七四十九日，三日后开丧送讣闻。这四十九日，单请一百单八众禅僧在大厅上拜大悲忏，超度前亡后化诸魂，以免亡者之罪；另设一坛于天香楼上，是九十九位全真道士，打四十九日解冤洗业醮。然后停灵于会芳园中，灵前另有五十众高僧、五十众高道，对坛按七作好事。那贾敬闻得长孙媳妇死了，因自为早晚就要飞升，如何肯又回家染了红尘，将前功尽弃呢，因此并不在意，只凭贾珍料理。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Jia Zhen struck his hands together. ‘How are they to be made? I shall simply give everything I have!’
As he spoke, Qin Ye and Qin Zhong arrived, together with several of You-shi’s relations, including her sisters. Jia Zhen told Jia Qiong, Jia Chen, Jia Lin and Jia Qiang to attend to the guests, and sent for an official from the Yin-yang Office of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau to select the dates. It was duly determined that the coffin should remain for seven times seven, forty-nine days, with formal mourning and the dispatch of notices to begin three days later. For those forty-nine days, a hundred and eight Chan monks alone were engaged to perform the Great Compassion repentance rite in the main hall, delivering the souls of those who had died before and those who would die hereafter, and absolving the dead of their sins. A separate altar was set up in the Tower of Heavenly Fragrance, where ninety-nine Quanzhen Taoist priests were to conduct, for forty-nine days, a Taoist offering rite to reconcile grievances and cleanse karmic burdens. The coffin was then placed in the Garden of Gathered Fragrance. Before it, another fifty eminent monks and fifty eminent Taoist priests performed rites at facing altars at each seven-day observance.
When Jia Jing heard that his eldest grandson’s wife had died, he was so certain that he himself would soon ascend to immortality that he could not possibly return home to be tainted by worldly dust and throw away all his previous efforts. He therefore paid little attention, leaving everything to Jia Zhen.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾珍见父亲不管，亦发恣意奢华。看板时，几副杉木板皆不中用。可巧薛蟠来吊问，因见贾珍寻好板，便说道：“我们木店里有一副板，叫做什么樯木，出在潢海铁网山上，作了棺材，万年不坏。这还是当年先父带来，原系义忠亲王老千岁要的，因他坏了事，就不曾拿去。现今还封在店里，也没人出价敢买。你若要，就抬来罢了。”贾珍听了，喜之不尽，即命人抬来。大家看时，只见帮底皆厚八寸，纹若槟榔，味若檀麝，以手扣之，玎珰如金玉。大家都奇异称赏。贾珍笑问：“价值几何？”薛蟠笑道：“拿一千两银子来，只怕也没处买去。什么价不价，赏他们几两工钱就是了。”贾珍听说，忙谢不尽，即命解锯糊漆。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
With his father taking no part, Jia Zhen indulged all the more freely in extravagant display. Several sets of fir boards were inspected for the coffin, but none was good enough. Xue Pan happened to come to pay his condolences and, seeing Jia Zhen in search of fine timber, said, ‘There is a set of boards in our timber shop. The wood is called qiang, or something of the sort. It comes from Iron-net Mountain in the Huang Sea region. Make a coffin of it and it will last ten thousand years without rotting. My late father brought it back years ago. His Highness Prince Yi-zhong originally wanted it, but when things went wrong for him, he never took delivery. It is still sealed up in the shop. Nobody has dared offer a price for it. If you want it, have it brought over.’
Jia Zhen was overjoyed and immediately ordered it to be fetched. When it arrived, they saw that the boards for the sides and bottom were all eight cun thick. Their grain resembled areca nut, their scent sandalwood and musk. Tapped with the hand, they rang like metal or jade. Everyone marvelled and praised them.
‘What is the price?’ Jia Zhen asked, smiling.
Xue Pan smiled too. ‘Even with a thousand taels of silver, you might not find anything like it. Why talk of a price? Just give the men a few taels for their trouble.’
Jia Zhen thanked him repeatedly and at once ordered the sawing, pasting and lacquering to begin.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 四大部州至中之地，奉天承运太平之国，总理虚无寂静教门僧录司正堂万虚、总理元始三一教门道录司正堂叶生等，敬谨修斋，朝天叩佛”，以及“恭请诸伽蓝、揭谛、功曹等神，圣恩普锡，神威远镇，四十九日消灾洗业平安水陆道场”等语，亦不消繁记。
earlier_text_evidence.english: ‘Here in the central land of the Four Great Continents, in this realm of peace which reverently receives Heaven’s mandate, Wan-xu, Chief of the Buddhist Registry, presiding over the teaching of emptiness and stillness, and Ye Sheng, Chief of the Taoist Registry, presiding over the teaching of the Primordial Origin and the Three-in-One, and their fellows, reverently perform the fasting rites, bowing to Heaven and prostrating themselves before the Buddha.’ There were also such passages as ‘Respectfully inviting the monastery guardians, the jiedi and the divine officers of merit’, and ‘May sacred grace be spread over all, and divine might hold distant evils in check: a Water-and-Land rite of forty-nine days to dispel calamity, cleanse karmic burdens and bring peace.’ We need not record it all.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 天天于卯正二刻就过来点卯理事，独在抱厦内起坐，不与众妯娌合群，便有堂客来往，也不迎会。这日乃五七正五日上，那应佛僧正开方破狱，传灯照亡，参阎君，拘都鬼，延请地藏王，开金桥，引幢幡；那道士们正伏章申表，朝三清，叩玉帝；禅僧们行香，放焰口，拜水忏；又有十三众尼僧，搭绣衣，趿红鞋，在灵前默诵接引诸咒，十分热闹。那凤姐必知今日人客不少，在家中歇宿一夜，至寅正，平儿便请起来梳洗。及收拾完备，更衣盥手，吃了几口奶子糖粳粥，漱口已毕，已是卯正二刻了。来旺媳妇率领诸人伺候已久。凤姐出至厅前，上了车，前面打了一对明角灯，大书“荣国府”三个大字，款款来至宁府。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Every day she arrived at half past six in the morning to call the roll and attend to business. She kept to the annex on her own instead of joining the other married women of the family, and did not go out to receive the visiting ladies either. This was the principal day of the fifth seventh-day observance. The Buddhist ritual monks were opening the ways and breaking open the prisons of hell, passing the lamps to light the dead on their way, paying homage to the Lord of the Underworld, summoning the ghost commanders, inviting Kshitigarbha, opening the golden bridge and leading the sacred banners. The Taoists were submitting their memorials and petitions, worshipping the Three Pure Ones and bowing before the Jade Emperor. The Chan monks were offering incense, performing the rite for feeding hungry ghosts and making their devotions in the Water Repentance rite. There were also thirteen Buddhist nuns, wearing embroidered robes and red shoes, silently reciting before the coffin the spells that would guide the departed. It was a scene of great activity.
Xi-feng knew there would be many visitors that day. Having spent the night at home, she was called by Patience in the middle of the yin hour to rise and make her toilette. By the time she was ready, had changed her clothes and washed her hands, eaten a few mouthfuls of rice gruel with milk and sugar, and rinsed her mouth, it was already half past six. Lai Wang-er’s wife and the other attendants had long been waiting. Xi-feng came out before the hall and got into her carriage. A pair of translucent horn lanterns went ahead, bearing three large Chinese characters meaning ‘Rong Mansion’, and the carriage moved at a measured pace to the Ning mansion.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 凤姐因见张材家的在旁，因问：“你有什么事？”张材家的忙取帖儿回说：“就是方才车轿围作成，领取裁缝工银若干两。”凤姐听了，便收了帖子，命彩明登记。待王兴家的交过牌，得了买办的回押相符，然后方与张材家的去领。一面又命念那一个，是为宝玉外书房完竣，支买纸料糊裱。凤姐听了，即命收帖儿登记，待张材家的缴清，又发与这人去了。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Seeing Zhang Cai’s wife standing nearby, Xi-feng asked what she wanted. The woman hurried to produce her slip. ‘It’s for the carriage and sedan-chair covers just finished, ma’am. So many taels for the tailors’ work.’ Xi-feng took the slip and told Sunshine to record it. Only after Wang Xing’s wife had returned the tally and the buyer’s countersigned receipt had been checked against it did she give it to Zhang Cai’s wife to collect the money. She then had the remaining slip read. Bao-yu’s outer study had been completed and paper was needed for lining and papering it. She ordered the slip to be kept and the entry made. When Zhang Cai’s wife had cleared her account and returned the tally, she issued it to this applicant in turn.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 走不多时，路旁彩棚高搭，设席张筵，和音奏乐，俱是各家路祭：第一座是王府东平王府祭棚，第二座是南安郡王祭棚，第三座是西宁郡王，第四座是北静郡王的。原来这四王，当日惟北静王功高，及今子孙犹袭王爵。现今北静王水溶年未弱冠，生得形容秀美，性情谦和。近闻宁国公冢孙媳告殂，因想当日彼此祖父相与之情，同难同荣，未以异姓相视，因此不以王位自居，上日也曾探丧上祭，如今又设路祭，命麾下的各官在此伺候。自己五更入朝，公事一毕，便换了素服，坐大轿鸣锣张伞而来，至棚前落轿。手下各官两旁拥侍，军民人众不得往还。
earlier_text_evidence.english: They had not gone far before they came upon tall, brightly decorated pavilions beside the road, with feasting tables laid and harmonious music playing. These were the different families’ roadside funeral offerings. The first was the mourning pavilion of the Prince of Dongping’s household, the second that of the Prince of Nan’an, the third that of the Prince of Xining and the fourth that of the Prince of Beijing. Of these four princes, the Prince of Beijing alone had rendered such great services in former days that his descendants still inherited the princely title. Its present holder, Shui Rong, was not yet twenty, handsome in appearance and gentle in disposition. Hearing lately of the death of the wife of the Duke of Ning’s eldest grandson, he had thought of the friendship between their grandfathers, who had shared hardship and glory and never treated one another as men of different surnames. He therefore set aside his princely dignity. He had already visited the house of mourning and made offerings, and now had roadside offerings prepared as well, ordering the officials under him to wait here. He himself had attended court during the fifth watch. As soon as his official business was over he changed into plain clothes and came in his great sedan-chair, with gongs sounding and a ceremonial parasol borne before him. He alighted in front of the pavilion. His officers crowded about him on either side, and neither soldiers nor civilians were allowed to pass.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 第十四回 林如海捐馆扬州城 贾宝玉路谒北静王
外面旺儿预备下赏封，赏了那本村主人，庄妇等来叩赏。凤姐并不在意，宝玉却留心看时，内中并没有二丫头。一时上了车，出来走不多远，只见迎头二丫头怀里抱着他小兄弟，同着几个小女孩子说笑而来。宝玉恨不得下车跟了他去，料是众人不依的，少不得以目相送，争奈车轻马快，一时展眼无踪。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Outside, Wang-er had prepared packets of gratuities and handed them to the owner of the farmstead. The farm women came to kowtow in thanks. Xi-feng paid no particular attention, but Bao-yu looked carefully: Second Girl was not among them. They got into the carriage and had not gone far when they saw her coming towards them, carrying her little brother and laughing and talking with several young girls. Bao-yu longed to get down and follow her, but he knew the others would never allow it. He could only follow her with his eyes. The carriage was light, the horses swift: in a moment she had vanished from sight.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾政等不知是何兆头。只得急忙更衣入朝。贾母等合家人等心中皆惶惶不定，不住的使人飞马来往探信。有两个时辰工夫，忽见赖大等三四个管家喘吁吁跑进仪门报喜，又说“奉老爷命，速请老太太带领太太等进朝谢恩”等语。那时贾母正心神不定，在大堂廊下伫立，那邢夫人、王夫人、尤氏、李纨、凤姐、迎春姊妹以及薛姨妈等皆在一处，听如此信至，贾母便唤进赖大来细问端的。赖大禀道：“小的们只在临敬门外伺候，里头的信息一概不能得知。后来还是夏太监出来道喜，说咱们家大小姐晋封为凤藻宫尚书，加封贤德妃。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Jia Zheng and the others could not tell what this portended. He could only hurry to change his clothes and go to court. Grandmother Jia and the whole family remained in an agony of uncertainty, constantly sending riders back and forth for news. About two double-hours had passed when three or four stewards, including Lai Da, came panting through the ceremonial gate with congratulations. Their master had ordered them to ask Her Old Ladyship to bring the ladies to court at once to give thanks for the imperial favour.

Grandmother Jia was standing anxiously under the verandah of the main hall. Lady Xing, Lady Wang, You-shi, Li Wan, Xi-feng, Ying-chun and her sisters, and Aunt Xue were all together there. On hearing the news, she called Lai Da in and questioned him closely.

‘We were waiting outside the Gate of Reverent Attendance,’ he reported, ‘and could learn nothing of what was going on within. At last the eunuch Xia came out to congratulate us. He said our eldest young lady had been promoted to Secretary of the Phoenix Splendour Palace, with the further title of Consort of Worthy Virtue.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 你回去说这样很好，若老爷们再要改时，全仗大爷谏阻，万不可另寻地方。明日一早我给大爷去请安去，再议细主。”贾蓉忙应几个“是”。贾蔷又近前回说：“下姑苏聘请教习，采买女孩子，置办乐器行头等事，大爷派了侄儿，带领着来管家两个儿子，还有单聘仁、卜固修两个清客相公，一同前去，所以命我来见叔叔。”贾琏听了，将贾蔷打谅了打谅，笑道：“你能在这一行么？这个事虽不算甚大，里头大有藏掖的。”贾蔷笑道：“只好学习着办罢了。”
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘Tell him I think this is excellent. If the masters want to change their minds, we must rely on him to dissuade them. On no account should we look elsewhere. I’ll come over early tomorrow to pay my respects and discuss the details.’

Jia Rong repeatedly assented. Jia Qiang now stepped forward.

‘Uncle, Master Zhen has put me in charge of going to Suzhou to engage instructors, buy girls and provide instruments, costumes and the rest. I’m to take the steward Lai’s two sons, and the two literary gentlemen Shan Pin-ren and Bu Gu-xiu. That’s why he told me to come and see you.’

Jia Lian looked him up and down and smiled.

‘Do you know anything about that line of business? It’s not a particularly large undertaking, but there are plenty of things hidden under the surface.’

‘I can only learn as I go,’ Jia Qiang said, smiling.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾政不惯于俗务，只凭贾赦、贾珍、贾琏、赖大、来升、林之孝、吴新登、詹光、程日兴等几人安插摆布。凡堆山凿池，起楼竖阁，种竹裁花，一应点景等事，又有山子野制度。下朝闲暇，不过各处看望看望，最要紧处和贾赦等商议商议便罢了。贾赦只在家高卧，有芥豆之事，贾珍等或自去回明，或写略节；或有话说，便传呼贾琏、赖大等来领命。贾蓉单管打造金银器皿。贾蔷已起身往姑苏去了。贾珍、赖大等又点人丁，开册籍，监工等事，一笔不能写到，不过一时喧阗热闹非常而已。暂且无话。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Jia Zheng was unused to practical business and left the arrangements entirely to Jia She, Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, Lai Da, Lai Sheng, Lin Zhi-xiao, Wu Xin-deng, Zhan Guang, Cheng Ri-xing and the others. Shan Zi-ye designed the artificial hills and excavated pools, the towers and pavilions, the planting of bamboos and flowers, and every other feature of the landscape. When free after court, Jia Zheng merely looked round the various parts and discussed the most important points with Jia She and the rest. Jia She himself stayed comfortably at home. Jia Zhen and the others reported every trifling matter to him, either in person or in a brief written account. If he had anything to say, he sent for Jia Lian, Lai Da and the others to receive his instructions. Jia Rong’s sole charge was the making of gold and silver vessels. Jia Qiang had already left for Suzhou. Jia Zhen, Lai Da and the rest also had to assign the workers, draw up registers and supervise the work. No single pen could describe it all. Enough to say that for a time there was extraordinary bustle and commotion. Let us leave them there.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 又有古人诗云：‘柴门临水稻花香。’何不就用‘稻香村’的妙？”众人听了，亦发哄声拍手道：“妙！”贾政一声喝断：“无知的业障！
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘Another old poet wrote, “A brushwood gate beside the water, rice blossom sweet in the air.” Why not call it “Sweet-rice Village”?’
They applauded with an even louder chorus of ‘Excellent!’
Jia Zheng cut them short with a shout.
‘Ignorant little curse!

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 第十七回 大观园试才题对额 荣国府归省庆元宵

此时王夫人那边热闹非常。原来贾蔷已从姑苏采买了十二个女孩子，并聘了教习，以及行头等事来了。那时薛姨妈另迁于东北上一所幽静房舍居住，将梨香院早已腾挪出来，另行修理了，就令教习在此教演女戏。又另派家中旧有曾演学过歌唱的众女人们，如今皆已皤然老妪了，着他们带领管理。就令贾蔷总理其日用出入银钱等事，以及诸凡大小所需之物料帐目。又有林之孝家的来回：“采访聘买的十个小尼姑、小道姑都有了，连新作的二十分道袍也有了。外有一个带发修行的，本是苏州人氏，祖上也是读书仕宦之家。因生了这位姑娘自小多病，买了许多替身儿皆不中用，到底这位姑娘亲自入了空门，方才好了，所以带发修行，今年才十八岁，法名妙玉。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Lady Wang’s quarters were a scene of great bustle. Jia Qiang had returned from Gusu with the twelve girls he had bought, the teachers he had engaged, and the theatrical costumes and other equipment. Aunt Xue had moved to a quiet set of rooms to the north-east. Pear-tree Court had long since been cleared and repaired, and the teachers were now to train the actresses there. Women of the household who had once learnt singing and performed themselves, but were now white-haired old women, had been appointed to supervise and look after them. Jia Qiang was put in charge of their daily expenditure and receipts, and the accounts for everything they required, large or small. Lin Zhi-xiao’s wife also came to report. ‘All ten of the young Buddhist and Taoist nuns we were to find and engage or buy are here, and the twenty sets of religious robes we ordered are ready too. There is one other young woman, practising the religious life without taking the tonsure. She comes from Suzhou, from a family of scholars and officials. She was always ill as a little girl. Her family bought any number of substitutes to enter religion in her place, but none did any good. Only when she entered the Buddhist life herself did she recover. That is why she practises without taking the tonsure. She is just eighteen this year, and her religious name is Adamantina.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 此一匾一联书于正殿。“大观园”园之名“有凤来仪”赐名曰“潇湘馆”。“红香绿玉”改作“怡红快绿”。即名曰“怡红院”。
earlier_text_evidence.english: This tablet and couplet were for the principal hall. ‘Prospect Garden’ was the name of the garden itself. ‘The Phoenix Comes in State’ was named ‘Naiad’s House’. ‘Red Fragrance and Green Jade’ became ‘Delight in Red and Joy in Green’, and the residence was named ‘House of Green Delights’.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: “蘅芷清芳”赐名曰“蘅芜苑”。“杏帘在望”赐名曰“浣葛山庄”。正楼曰“大观楼”，东面飞楼曰“缀锦阁”，西面斜楼曰“含芳阁”；更有“蓼风轩”、“藕香榭”、“紫菱洲”、“叶渚”等名；又有四字的匾额十数个，诸如“梨花春雨”、“桐剪秋风”、“荻芦夜雪”等名，此时悉难全记。又命旧有匾联者俱不必摘去。于是先题一绝云：
earlier_text_evidence.english: ‘Pure Scent of Heng and Zhi’ was named ‘Allspice Court’; ‘The Apricot Tavern Flag in Sight’ became ‘Kudzu-washing Grange’. The main tower was ‘Prospect Tower’, the soaring building to the east ‘Brocade-adorned Pavilion’, and the obliquely set building to the west ‘Fragrance-bearing Pavilion’. There were also such names as ‘Knotweed Breeze Pavilion’, ‘Lotus Pavilion’, ‘Amaryllis Eyot’ and ‘Leafy Islet’. More than ten further tablets had four-character inscriptions, among them ‘Pear Blossom in Spring Rain’, ‘Autumn Wind Cuts the Paulownia’ and ‘Night Snow on Reeds’; it is difficult to record them all here. She ordered that none of the existing tablets and couplets need be taken down. Then she began by writing this quatrain:

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 写毕，向诸姐妹笑道：“我素乏捷才，且不长于吟咏，妹辈素所深知。今夜聊以塞责，不负斯景而已。异日少暇，必补撰《大观园记》并《省亲颂》等文，以记今日之事。妹辈亦各题一匾一诗，随才之长短，亦暂吟成，不可因我微才所缚。且喜宝玉竟知题咏，是我意外之想。此中‘潇湘馆’、‘蘅芜院’二处，我所极爱，次之‘怡红院’、‘浣葛山庄’，此四大处，必得别有章句题咏方妙。前所题之联虽佳，如今再各赋五言律一首，使我当面试过，方不负我自幼教授之苦心。”宝玉只得答应了，下来自去构思。
earlier_text_evidence.english: When she had finished, she smiled at her sisters and cousins. ‘You all know very well that I have never been quick-witted, nor much good at verse. Tonight I have merely done what was required, so as not to fail such a setting. Some other day, when I have a little leisure, I must write an “Account of Prospect Garden”, an “Ode to the Imperial Home Visit” and other pieces to record this occasion. Each of you must also compose an inscription and a poem. Do the best you can on the spur of the moment, and do not let my poor efforts constrain you. I am delighted that Bao-yu has learnt to compose inscriptions and verse. It is more than I expected. Of these places, I love Naiad’s House and Allspice Court most, and next to them the House of Green Delights and Kudzu-washing Grange. These four principal sites deserve poems of their own. The couplets you wrote before were good, but now you must compose an eight-line poem in five-character lines for each. Let me test you here in person, and feel that the trouble I took over teaching you as a child was not wasted.’ Bao-yu could only agree. He withdrew to think.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾妃看毕，称赏一番，又笑道：“终是薛林二妹之作与众不同，非愚姊妹可同列者。”原来林黛玉安心今夜大展奇才，将众人压倒，不想贾妃只命一匾一咏，倒不好违谕多作，只胡乱作一首五律应景罢了。彼时宝玉尚未作完，只刚做了“潇湘馆”与“蘅芜苑”二首，正作“怡红院”一首，起草内有“绿玉春犹卷”一句。宝钗转眼瞥见，便趁众人不理论，急忙回身悄推他道：“他因不喜‘红香绿玉’四字，改了‘怡红快绿’；你这会子偏用‘绿玉’二字，岂不是有意和他争驰了？况且蕉叶之说也颇多，再想一个改了罢。”宝玉见宝钗如此说，便拭汗说道：“我这会子总想不起什么典故出处来。”宝钗笑道：“你只把‘绿玉’的‘玉’字改作‘蜡’字就是了。”宝玉道：“‘绿蜡’可有出处？”宝钗见问，悄悄的咂嘴点头
earlier_text_evidence.english: When the Consort had read them, she praised them all, then smiled. ‘Our Xue and Lin cousins’ poems are different from the rest, after all. We foolish sisters cannot rank with them.’ Dai-yu had intended to display her extraordinary gifts that evening and outshine everyone. But the Consort had ordered only one inscription and one poem apiece. She could hardly disobey by writing more, and had merely tossed off an eight-line poem in five-character lines to suit the occasion. Bao-yu had not yet finished. He had completed only the poems on Naiad’s House and Allspice Court and was working on the House of Green Delights. His draft contained the line ‘Green jade stays furled in spring’. Bao-chai caught sight of it. While the others were paying no attention, she quickly turned, nudged him, and whispered, ‘She disliked “Red Fragrance and Green Jade” and changed it to “Delight in Red and Joy in Green”. If you insist on “green jade” now, will it not look as though you mean to challenge her? There are plenty of other expressions for plantain leaves. Think of one and change it.’ Bao-yu wiped his brow. ‘I cannot remember a single allusion or source just now.’ Bao-chai smiled. ‘Just change the word “jade” in “green jade” to “wax”.’ ‘Is there a source for “green wax”?’ At his question, Bao-chai quietly clicked her tongue and nodded,

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾妃看毕，喜之不尽，说：“果然进益了！”又指“杏帘”一首为前三首之冠。遂将“浣葛山庄”改为“稻香村”。又命探春另以彩笺誊录出方才一共十数首诗，出令太监传与外厢。贾政等看了，都称颂不已。贾政又进《归省颂》。元妃又命以琼酥金脍等物，赐与宝玉并贾兰。此时贾兰极幼，未达诸事，只不过随母依叔行礼，故无别传。贾环从年内染病未痊，自有闲处调养，故亦无传。
earlier_text_evidence.english: The Consort was delighted with what she read. ‘He really has improved!’ She singled out ‘The Apricot Tavern Flag’ as better than the preceding three and changed ‘Kudzu-washing Grange’ to ‘Sweet-rice Village’. She then ordered Tan-chun to copy on coloured paper all the dozen or more poems just composed, and had a eunuch carry them to the men outside. Jia Zheng and the others read them with endless praise. Jia Zheng also presented an ‘Ode to the Homecoming’. The Consort ordered delicacies, including fine milk pastries and golden sliced fish, to be given to Bao-yu and Jia Lan. Jia Lan was still very young and understood little of what was happening. He merely followed his mother and kept close to his uncle to perform the ceremonies, so there is no separate account of him. Jia Huan, who had fallen ill before the New Year and had not recovered, was being nursed in a quiet place; there is therefore no account of him either.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 那时贾蔷带领十二个女戏，在楼下正等的不耐烦，只见一太监飞来说：“作完了诗，快拿戏目来！”贾蔷急将锦册呈上，并十二个花名单子。少时，太监出来，只点了四出戏：第一出《豪宴》；第二出《乞巧》；第三出《仙缘》；第四出《离魂》。贾蔷忙张罗扮演起来。一个个歌欺裂石之音，舞有天魔之态。虽是妆演的形容，却作尽悲欢情状。刚演完了，一太监执一金盘糕点之属进来，问：“谁是龄官？”贾蔷便知是赐龄官之物，喜的忙接了，命龄官叩头。太监又道：“贵妃有谕，说：‘龄官极好，再作两出戏，不拘那两出就是了。’”贾蔷忙答应了，因命龄官做《游园》、《惊梦》二出。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Meanwhile, Jia Qiang and the twelve actresses were waiting impatiently below the tower. A eunuch came hurrying up. ‘The poems are finished. Bring the list of plays at once!’ Jia Qiang hastily presented the brocade-covered programme, together with the roster of all twelve girls. Soon the eunuch returned. Only four scenes had been selected: first, ‘The Lavish Feast’; second, ‘Praying for Skill’; third, ‘An Immortal Encounter’; and fourth, ‘The Soul’s Departure’. Jia Qiang hurried to get the performers ready. Their singing outdid voices that could split stone, and they danced with the allure of heavenly demons. Though all was costume and acting, they conveyed every shade of sorrow and joy. They had just finished when a eunuch came in carrying a golden tray of cakes and other dainties. ‘Which is Ling-guan?’ he asked. Jia Qiang knew at once that these were gifts for her. Delighted, he hastened to receive them and told her to kowtow. ‘Her Highness commands,’ the eunuch continued, ‘“Ling-guan is excellent. Let her perform two more scenes, any two she pleases.”’ Jia Qiang eagerly agreed and told Ling-guan to perform ‘A Walk in the Garden’ and ‘A Dream Interrupted’.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 龄官自为此二出原非本角之戏，执意不作，定要作《相约》《相骂》二出。贾蔷扭他不过，只得依他作了。贾妃甚喜，命“不可难为了这女孩子，好生教习”，额外赏了两匹宫缎、两个荷包并金银锞子、食物之类。然后撤筵，将未到之处复又游顽。忽见山环佛寺，忙另盥手进去焚香拜佛，又题一匾云：“苦海慈航”。又额外加恩与一班幽尼女道。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Ling-guan considered neither scene proper to her own theatrical role and flatly refused. She insisted on ‘The Rendezvous’ and ‘The Quarrel’. Jia Qiang could not prevail against her and had to let her have her way. The Consort was delighted. ‘Do not make things difficult for this girl,’ she ordered. ‘See that she is well taught.’ She gave her an additional reward of two lengths of palace satin, two purses, small gold and silver ingots, food and other things. The banquet was then cleared away, and they toured the places they had not yet visited. Suddenly, seeing a Buddhist temple encircled by hills, the Consort had her hands washed afresh and went in to burn incense and worship. She wrote another tablet, ‘Mercy’s Vessel across the Sea of Suffering’, and bestowed additional favours on the secluded Buddhist and Taoist nuns.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 茗烟因问：“二爷为何不看这样的好戏？”宝玉道：“看了半日，怪烦的，出来逛逛，就遇见你们了。这会子作什么呢？”茗烟嘻嘻笑道：“这会子没人知道，我悄悄的引二爷往城外逛逛去，一会子再往这里来，他们就不知道了。”宝玉道：“不好，仔细花子拐了去。便是他们知道了，又闹大了，不如往熟近些的地方去，还可就来。”茗烟道：“熟近地方，谁家可去？这却难了。”宝玉笑道：“依我的主意，咱们竟找你花大姐姐去，瞧他在家作什么呢。”茗烟笑道：“好，好！倒忘了他家。”又道：“若他们知道了，说我引着二爷胡走，要打我呢？”宝玉笑道：“有我呢。”茗烟听说，拉了马，二人从后门就走了。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Tealeaf asked, ‘Why aren’t you watching such fine plays, Master Bao?’
‘I watched for ages and got dreadfully bored. I came out for a stroll and found the two of you. What shall we do now?’
Tealeaf grinned. ‘No one knows where we are. I could quietly take you outside the city for a look round, and we’d come back here in a little while. They’d never know.’
‘No. We might get carried off by beggars. And if they found out, there would be an awful fuss. We’d better go somewhere familiar and close by, where we can get back at once.’
‘Somewhere familiar and close by? Whose house could we go to? That’s a difficult one.’
‘I know,’ said Bao-yu, smiling. ‘Let’s go and find your big sister Hua, and see what she’s doing at home.’
‘Yes, yes!’ Tealeaf laughed. ‘I’d forgotten about her house. But if they find out and say I took you roaming about, won’t they beat me?’
‘You’ve got me,’ Bao-yu said with a smile.
At that Tealeaf brought the horses, and the two went out by the back gate.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 宝玉听说，只得替他去了簪环，看他躺下，自往上房来。同贾母吃毕饭，贾母犹欲同那几个老管家嬷嬷斗牌解闷，宝玉记着袭人，便回至房中，见袭人朦朦睡去。自己要睡，天气尚早。彼时晴雯、绮霰、秋纹、碧痕都寻热闹，找鸳鸯琥珀等耍戏去了，独见麝月一个人在外间房里灯下抹骨牌。宝玉笑问道：“你怎不同他们顽去？”麝月道：“没有钱。”宝玉道：“床底下堆着那么些，还不够你输的？”麝月道：“都顽去了，这屋里交给谁呢？那一个又病了。满屋里上头是灯，地下是火。那些老妈妈子们，老天拔地，伏侍一天，也该叫他们歇歇，小丫头子们也是伏侍了一天，这会子还不叫他们顽顽去。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Bao-yu could only do as she asked. He took off her hairpins and earrings, saw her lie down, and went to Grandmother Jia’s rooms. After they had eaten, she wanted to amuse herself at cards with the old senior serving-women, but he was thinking of Aroma and returned to his room. She had drifted into a doze. He thought of going to bed himself, but it was still too early.
Skybright, Mackerel, Ripple and Emerald had all gone off in search of amusement with Faithful, Amber and the others. Only Musk remained, laying out dominoes by lamplight in the outer room.
‘Why haven’t you gone to play with them?’ he asked, smiling.
‘I haven’t any money.’
‘There’s all that money piled under the bed. Isn’t that enough for you to lose?’
‘If everyone goes off to play, who’s to look after the room? She’s ill, too. There are lamps up above and fires down below, all over the place. Those poor old mammas, at their age, have been waiting on us all day. They ought to have a rest. And the little maids have been working all day too. If they can’t go and play now, when can they?

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: ——你道是何呆意？因他自幼姊妹丛中长大，亲姊妹有元春、探春，伯叔的有迎春、惜春，亲戚中又有史湘云、林黛玉、薛宝钗等诸人。他便料定，原来天生人为万物之灵，凡山川日月之精秀，只钟于女儿，须眉男子不过是些渣滓浊沫而已。因有这个呆念在心，把一切男子都看成混沌浊物，可有可无。只是父亲叔伯兄弟中。因孔子是亘古第一人说下的，不可忤慢，只得要听他这句话。所以，弟兄之间不过尽其大概的情理就罢了，并不想自己是丈夫，须要为子弟之表率。是以贾环等都不怕他，却怕贾母，才让他三分。如今宝钗恐怕宝玉教训他，倒没意思，便连忙替贾环掩饰。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
What foolish notion, you ask? From earliest childhood he had grown up among girls. There were his own sisters Yuan-chun and Tan-chun, his paternal cousins Ying-chun and Xi-chun, and other relations such as Shi Xiang-yun, Lin Dai-yu and Xue Bao-chai. He had therefore concluded that, though human beings were born the most spiritual of all creatures, the purest essence of mountains and rivers, sun and moon, was bestowed on girls alone. Bearded men were merely the dregs and dirty froth.
With this foolish notion in his head, he considered all males muddy, undifferentiated creatures whom one could quite well do without. There was an exception for his father, uncles and brothers: Confucius, the foremost man of all time, had said one must not defy or slight them, and Bao-yu could only obey his injunction. So, with his brothers, he did no more than observe the broad requirements of affection and propriety. He never thought that, as a man, he ought to set an example to the younger members of the family. Jia Huan and the rest were consequently not afraid of him, though fear of Grandmother Jia made them show him a little deference.
Now Bao-chai, afraid that a lecture from Bao-yu would only make matters awkward for Jia Huan, hastily made excuses for him.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 宝钗笑道：“等着，咱们两个一齐走，瞧瞧他去。”说着，下了炕，同宝玉一齐来至贾母这边。只见史湘云大笑大说的，见他两个来，忙问好厮见。正值林黛玉在旁，因问宝玉：“在那里的？”宝玉便说：“在宝姐姐家的。”黛玉冷笑道：“我说呢，亏在那里绊住，不然早就飞了来了。”宝玉笑道：“只许同你顽，替你解闷儿。不过偶然去他那里一趟，就说这话。”林黛玉道：“好没意思的话！去不去管我什么事，我又没叫你替我解闷儿。可许你从此不理我呢！”说着，便赌气回房去了。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘Wait,’ Bao-chai said with a smile. ‘Let’s go and see her together.’
She got down from the kang and went with him to Grandmother Jia’s rooms. They found Shi Xiang-yun talking and laughing at the top of her voice. When she saw the two of them, she hurried to exchange greetings. Dai-yu was there too.
‘Where have you been?’ she asked Bao-yu.
‘At Cousin Bao-chai’s.’
Dai-yu gave a cold laugh.
‘I thought as much. Lucky something kept you there, or you’d have flown here long ago.’
‘So I’m only allowed to play with you and keep you amused?’ Bao-yu said, smiling. ‘I go to see her once in a while, and this is what you say.’
‘What a tiresome thing to say! What do I care whether you go or not? I never asked you to keep me amused. You’re quite welcome never to speak to me again!’
With that, she went back to her room in a huff.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 黛玉道：“我不依。你们是一气的，都戏弄我不成！”宝玉劝道：“谁敢打趣你！你不打趣他，他焉敢说你？”四人正难分解，有人来请吃饭，方往前边来。那天早又掌灯时分，王夫人、李纨、凤姐、迎、探、惜等都往贾母这边来，大家闲话了一回，各自归寝。湘云仍往黛玉房中安歇。宝玉送他二人到房，那天已二更多时，袭人来催了几次，方回自己房中来睡。次日天明时，便披衣靸鞋往黛玉房中来，不见紫鹃、翠缕二人，只见他姊妹两个尚卧在衾内。那林黛玉严严密密裹着一幅杏子红绫被，安稳合目而睡。那史湘云却一把青丝拖于枕畔，被只齐胸，一弯雪白的膀子撂于被外，又带着两个金镯子。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘I won’t!’ Dai-yu said. ‘You’re all in league against me. Do you mean to make fun of me together?’
‘Who would dare make fun of you?’ Bao-yu coaxed. ‘If you hadn’t teased her, would she have dared say anything about you?’
The four were still at an impasse when someone came to call them to dinner, and only then did they go to the front rooms. By lamplighting time that evening, Lady Wang, Li Wan, Xi-feng, Ying-chun, Tan-chun, Xi-chun and the others had all come to Grandmother Jia’s. They chatted for a while, then went their separate ways to bed. Xiang-yun again slept in Dai-yu’s room. Bao-yu saw the two of them back to their room. It was well into the second watch, and Aroma had come several times to hurry him, before he returned to his own room to sleep.
At daybreak he threw on his clothes, slipped his feet into his shoes and went over to Dai-yu’s room. Neither Nightingale nor Kingfisher was there. The two cousins were still in bed. Dai-yu lay peacefully asleep, her eyes closed, wrapped snugly in an apricot-red figured-silk quilt. Xiang-yun’s black hair trailed beside her pillow; her quilt came only to her chest, and a snow-white arm curved outside it, with two gold bracelets on it.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 且说那个玉皇庙并达摩庵两处，一班的十二个小沙弥并十二个小道士，如今挪出大观园来，贾政正想发到各庙去分住。不想后街上住的贾芹之母周氏，正盘算着也要到贾政这边谋一个大小事务与儿子管管，也好弄些银钱使用，可巧听见这件事出来，便坐轿子来求凤姐。凤姐因见他素日不大拿班作势的，便依允了，想了几句话便回王夫人说：“这些小和尚道士万不可打发到别处去，一时娘娘出来就要承应。倘或散了，若再用时，可是又费事。依我的主意，不如将他们竟送到咱们家庙里铁槛寺去，月间不过派一个人拿几两银子去买柴米就完了。说声用，走去叫来，一点儿不费事呢。”王夫人听了，便商之于贾政。

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 一面安慰，一面唤了两个老嬷嬷来，吩咐：“好生带了宝玉去，别叫他老子唬着他。”老嬷嬷答应了。宝玉只得前去，一步挪不了三寸，蹭到这边来。可巧贾政在王夫人房中商议事情，金钏儿、彩云、彩霞、绣鸾、绣凤等众丫鬟都在廊檐底下站着呢，一见宝玉来，都抿着嘴笑。金钏一把拉住宝玉，悄悄的笑道：“我这嘴上是才擦的香浸胭脂，你这会子可吃不吃了？”彩云一把推开金钏，笑道：“人家正心里不自在，你还奚落他。趁这会子喜欢，快进去罢。”
earlier_text_evidence.english:

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 谁想静中生烦恼，忽一日不自在起来，这也不好，那也不好，出来进去只是闷闷的。园中那些人多半是女孩儿，正在混沌世界，天真烂漫之时，坐卧不避，嘻笑无心，那里知宝玉此时的心事。那宝玉心内不自在，便懒在园内，只在外头鬼混，却又痴痴的。茗烟见他这样，因想与他开心，左思右想，皆是宝玉顽烦了的，不能开心，惟有这件，宝玉不曾看见过。想毕，便走去到书坊内，把那古今小说并那飞燕、合德、武则天、杨贵妃的外传与那传奇角本买了许多来，引宝玉看。宝玉何曾见过这些书，一看见了便如得了珍宝。茗烟嘱咐他不可拿进园去，“若叫人知道了，我就吃不了兜着走呢。”宝玉那里舍的不拿进园去，踟蹰再三，单把那文理细密的拣了几套进去，放在床顶上，无人时自己密看。

Who would have thought that vexation could spring from such tranquillity? One day Bao-yu suddenly grew dissatisfied. Nothing was right, neither this nor that; indoors or out, he was always miserable. Most of the people in the garden were young girls, still in a world of unawakened, carefree innocence. They sat or lay down without reserve, laughed without a thought behind it: how could they know what was on Bao-yu’s mind? In his discontent he lost the inclination to stay in the garden and spent his time idling about outside, still in a daze. Seeing him like this, Tealeaf wanted to cheer him up. But every amusement he thought of was something Bao-yu had already tired of, and would give him no pleasure. There was just one thing Bao-yu had never seen. Having thought of it, Tealeaf went to a bookshop and bought a great many novels old and new, unofficial lives of Flying Swallow, He-de, Wu Ze-tian and Noble Consort Yang, and scripts of romance plays. He tempted Bao-yu to read them. Bao-yu had never seen books of this kind, and the moment he did, he felt he had found a treasure. Tealeaf warned him not to take them into the garden.
‘If anyone finds out, I’ll get more than I bargained for.’
But how could Bao-yu bear not to take them in? After much hesitation, he selected a few sets with the more subtle, carefully wrought writing, took them into the garden and put them above his bed, to read in secret when no one was there.
