‘Tomorrow I’ll tell the others,’ Emerald said. ‘Whenever there’s tea or water wanted, or anything to be carried in or out, none of us need stir. Let her do it all.’
‘In that case,’ said Ripple, ‘we might as well all go away and leave her alone in his rooms.’
They were still keeping up this barrage, one after the other, when an old woman came in with a message from Xi-feng.
‘Someone will be bringing gardeners in to plant trees tomorrow. You’re to be more careful. Don’t leave your jackets and skirts hanging out to dry all over the place. That whole stretch along the artificial hill is being screened off with hangings. Don’t go running about where you please.’
‘Do you know who’s bringing the workmen in to supervise them?’ Ripple asked.
‘Someone called Master Yun, from the rear lane.’
Neither Ripple nor Emerald knew him, and they went on asking all sorts of other questions.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 那小红听见了，心内却明白，就知是昨儿外书房所见那人了。原来这小红本姓林，小名红玉，只因“玉”字犯了林黛玉、宝玉，便都把这个字隐起来，便都叫他“小红”。原是荣国府中世代的旧仆，他父母现在收管各处房田事务。这红玉年方十六岁，因分人在大观园的时节，把他便分在怡红院中，倒也清幽雅静。不想后来命人进来居住，偏生这一所儿又被宝玉占了。这红玉虽然是个不谙事的丫头，却因他有三分容貌，心内着实妄想痴心的往上攀高，每每的要在宝玉面前现弄现弄。只是宝玉身边一干人，都是伶牙利爪的，那里插的下手去。不想今儿才有些消息，又遭秋纹等一场恶意，心内早灰了一半。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Crimson, however, understood at once: it was the young man she had seen in the outer study yesterday.
Her surname was Lin and her childhood name Hong-yu, ‘red jade’. But because the ‘yu’, or ‘jade’, encroached on the names of Lin Dai-yu and Bao-yu, everyone had dropped that part and called her simply Crimson. Her family had served the Rong mansion for generations, and her parents now managed the houses and land in various places. She was only sixteen. When servants were being assigned to Prospect Garden, she had been sent to the House of Green Delights, where life was quiet and secluded enough. But then came the order for people to move into the garden, and Bao-yu happened to be given that very house.
Inexperienced girl though she was, Crimson had a certain prettiness and an earnest, foolish longing to rise in the world. Time and again she wanted to show what she could do in front of Bao-yu. But all the people about him had sharp tongues and ready claws. Where could she find a place among them? Today, unexpectedly, she had at last had a little opening, only to meet this spiteful attack from Ripple and the others. Already half her hopes had turned to ashes.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 正闷闷的，忽然听见老嬷嬷说起贾芸来，不觉心中一动，便闷闷的回至房中，睡在床上暗暗盘算，翻来掉去，正没个抓寻。忽听窗外低低的叫道：“红玉，你的手帕子我拾在这里呢。”红玉听了忙走出来看，不是别人，正是贾芸。红玉不觉的粉面含羞，问道：“二爷在那里拾着的？”贾芸笑道：“你过来，我告诉你。”一面说，一面就上来拉他。那红玉急回身一跑，却被门槛绊倒。要知端的，下回分解。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
She was brooding over it when the old woman’s mention of Jia Yun stirred something in her heart. Still troubled, she returned to her room and lay on the bed thinking it over in secret, turning this way and that without knowing what to do.
Suddenly a low voice called outside the window, ‘Crimson, I’ve found your handkerchief. I have it here.’
She hurried out to look. It was none other than Jia Yun. Her fair face coloured with bashfulness.
‘Where did you find it, sir?’
‘Come here and I’ll tell you,’ Jia Yun said with a smile, reaching out to take hold of her as he spoke.
Crimson turned quickly to run, but caught her foot on the threshold and fell.
To learn what really happened, you must read the next chapter.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 话说红玉心神恍惚，情思缠绵，忽朦胧睡去，遇见贾芸要拉他，却回身一跑，被门槛绊了一跤，唬醒过来，方知是梦。因此翻来复去，一夜无眠。至次日天明，方才起来，就有几个丫头子来会他去打扫房子地面，提洗脸水。这红玉也不梳洗，向镜中胡乱挽了一挽头发，洗了洗手，腰内束了一条汗巾子，便来打扫房屋。谁知宝玉昨儿见了红玉，也就留了心。若要直点名唤他来使用，一则怕袭人等寒心；二则又不知红玉是何等行为，若好还罢了，若不好起来，那时倒不好退送的。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Now Crimson, her mind wandering and her thoughts entangled in love, had drifted off to sleep. She met Jia Yun, who tried to take hold of her; turning to run, she tripped over the threshold and fell. The fright woke her, and only then did she realise it had been a dream. She tossed and turned after that, unable to sleep all night. At daybreak she got up. Several of the other maids came to fetch her to sweep the rooms and floors and carry water for washing. Without stopping to wash her face or comb her hair properly, she twisted up her hair anyhow before the mirror, washed her hands, tied a cloth round her waist and went to clean the rooms.
Bao-yu, meanwhile, had noticed Crimson the day before and had not forgotten her. He could have called for her by name to wait on him, but for two things: first, he was afraid of hurting Aroma and the others; and second, he did not yet know what sort of girl Crimson was. If she turned out well, all would be well; if she did not, it would be awkward to send her back.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 可巧王夫人见贾环下了学，便命他来抄个《金刚咒》唪诵唪诵。那贾环正在王夫人炕上坐着，命人点灯，拿腔作势的抄写。一时又叫彩云倒杯茶来，一时又叫玉钏儿来剪剪蜡花，一时又说金钏儿挡了灯影。众丫鬟们素日厌恶他，都不答理。只有彩霞还和他合的来，倒了一钟茶来递与他。因见王夫人和人说话儿，他便悄悄的向贾环说道：“你安些分罢，何苦讨这个厌那个厌的。”贾环道：“我也知道了，你别哄我。如今你和宝玉好，把我不答理，我也看出来了。”彩霞咬着嘴唇，向贾环头上戳了一指头，说道：“没良心的！狗咬吕洞宾，不识好人心。”
earlier_text_evidence.english:
As it happened, when Jia Huan came home from school, Lady Wang had told him to copy out the Vajra Mantra and recite it. He was now sitting on her kang, ordering the lamps to be lit and making a great show of his copying. One moment he called to Cai-yun to pour him a cup of tea, the next to Silver to trim a candle; then he complained that Golden was standing in his light. The maids, who had always disliked him, took no notice. Only Cai-xia was still on good terms with him. She poured a cup of tea and handed it to him, and, seeing Lady Wang occupied in conversation, spoke to him quietly.
‘Do behave yourself. Why must you make everyone dislike you?’
‘I know all about it,’ said Jia Huan. ‘Don’t try to fool me. You’re friendly with Bao-yu now and won’t have anything to do with me. I’ve seen it for myself.’
Cai-xia bit her lip and poked him in the forehead.
‘Ungrateful thing! You’re like the dog that bit Lü Dong-bin: you don’t know a kind heart when you find one.’

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 宝玉道：“也不很疼，养一两日就好了。”林黛玉坐了一回，闷闷的回房去了。一宿无话。次日，宝玉见了贾母，虽然自己承认是自己烫的，不与别人相干，免不得那贾母又把跟从的人骂一顿。过了一日，就有宝玉寄名的干娘马道婆进荣国府来请安。见了宝玉，唬一大跳，问起原由，说是烫的，便点头叹息一回，向宝玉脸上用指头画了一画，口内嘟囔囔的又持诵了一回，说道：“管保就好了，这不过是一时飞灾。”又向贾母道：“祖宗老菩萨那里知道，那经典佛法上说的利害，大凡那王公卿相人家的子弟，只一生长下来，暗里便有许多促狭鬼跟着他，得空便拧他一下，或掐他一下，或吃饭时打下他的饭碗来，或走着推他一跤，所以往往的那些大家子孙多有长不大的。”贾母听如此说，便赶着问：“这有什么佛法解释没有呢？”马道婆道：“这个容易，只是替他多作些因果善事也就罢了。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘Not very much. A day or two’s rest will put it right,’ said Bao-yu.
Dai-yu sat for a while, then returned unhappily to her own rooms. Nothing more need be said of that night. Next day Bao-yu went to see Grandmother Jia. Although he declared that he had burnt himself and that no one else was to blame, she duly scolded his attendants all the same.
Another day passed, and Mother Ma, to whom Bao-yu had been entrusted as a godson for spiritual protection, came to pay her respects at the Rong mansion. The sight of him gave her a great start. She asked what had happened, and when told of the burn, nodded and sighed for a while, traced a figure with her finger on his face, and muttered prayers over him.
‘It’s certain to get better. This is only a passing stroke of misfortune.’
Then she turned to Grandmother Jia.
‘Your Old Ladyship, our venerable living Bodhisattva, can have no notion of the terrible things described in the Buddhist scriptures. From the moment a child is born into the family of a prince or a great minister, there are mischievous little demons following him unseen. Whenever they get a chance they give him a twist or a pinch, knock his bowl from his hand as he eats, or trip him up as he walks. That is why so many children in great families never live to grow up.’
‘Is there no Buddhist remedy for it?’ Grandmother Jia asked at once.
‘That’s easy enough,’ said Mother Ma. ‘You need only do more good works on his behalf, to bring him a good return.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 再那经上还说，西方有位大光明普照菩萨，专管照耀阴暗邪祟，若有善男子善女子虔心供奉者，可以永佑儿孙康宁安静，再无惊恐邪祟撞客之灾。“贾母道：”倒不知怎么个供奉这位菩萨？“马道婆道：”也不值些什么，不过除香烛供养之外，一天多添几斤香油，点上个大海灯。这海灯，便是菩萨现身法像，昼夜不敢息的。“贾母道：”一天一夜也得多少油？明白告诉我，我也好作这件功德的。“马道婆听如此说，便笑道：”这也不拘，随施主菩萨们随心愿舍罢了。像我们庙里，就有好几处的王妃诰命供奉的：南安郡王府里的太妃，他许的多，愿心大，一天是四十八斤油，一斤灯草，那海灯也只比缸略小些；锦田侯的诰命次一等，一天不过二十四斤油；再还有几家也有五斤的、三斤的、一斤的，都不拘数。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘The scriptures also tell of the Bodhisattva of Great All-Illuminating Light in the West, whose special charge is to shine into the darkness where evil spirits lurk. Any devout man or woman who makes offerings with a sincere heart can secure lasting health and peace for their children and grandchildren, with no more harm from frights, evil spirits or possessing ghosts.’
‘But how does one make offerings to this Bodhisattva?’ asked Grandmother Jia.
‘It costs very little. Besides the incense and candles, one need only provide a few jin of fragrant oil every day to keep a great votive lamp burning. The votive lamp is the Bodhisattva’s own manifested image, and must never be allowed to go out, day or night.’
‘How much oil does it take for a day and a night? Tell me plainly, so that I too can earn this merit.’
At this Mother Ma smiled.
‘There’s no fixed amount. Our benefactors, those living Bodhisattvas, give just as their hearts move them. Several princely consorts and titled ladies make such offerings at our temple. The dowager consort of the Prince of Nan’an’s household has made a great vow and gives generously: forty-eight jin of oil and one jin of wick-rushes every day. Her votive lamp is only a little smaller than a vat. The titled wife of the Marquis of Jintian gives on a somewhat smaller scale, only twenty-four jin of oil a day. Others give five jin, or three, or one. There is no fixed quantity.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 那小家子穷人家舍不起这些，就是四两半斤，也少不得替他点。“贾母听了，点头思忖。马道婆又道：”还有一件，若是为父母尊亲长上的，多舍些不妨；若是象老祖宗如今为宝玉，若舍多了倒不好，还怕哥儿禁不起，倒折了福。也不当家花花的，要舍，大则七斤，小则五斤，也就是了。“贾母说：”既是这样说，你便一日五斤合准了，每月打趸来关了去。“马道婆念了一声”阿弥陀佛慈悲大菩萨“。贾母又命人来吩咐：”以后大凡宝玉出门的日子，拿几串钱交给他的小子们带着，遇见僧道穷苦人好舍。“说毕，那马道婆又坐了一回，便又往各院各房问安，闲逛了一回。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘Poor people in small households cannot afford so much. Even if they give only four taels of oil or half a jin, we still have to light a lamp for them.’
Grandmother Jia nodded thoughtfully.
‘There’s another thing,’ Mother Ma went on. ‘For one’s parents or honoured elders, it does no harm to give more. But when Your Old Ladyship is giving for Bao-yu, too much might be a bad thing. The young gentleman might not be able to bear it, and his blessings would be diminished instead. Besides, there’s no need to spend the household money so freely. If you wish to make an offering, seven jin at the most, or five at the least, will do perfectly well.’
‘In that case,’ said Grandmother Jia, ‘settle it at five jin a day. You can come and draw the whole month’s allowance at once.’
‘Amitabha, merciful great Bodhisattva!’ Mother Ma intoned.
Grandmother Jia then called in a servant and gave further instructions.
‘From now on, whenever Bao-yu goes out, give his pages a few strings of cash to take with them, so that he can give alms to any monks, Taoists or poor people he meets.’
Mother Ma sat a little longer, then wandered about paying her respects in the other courtyards and apartments.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 一时来至赵姨娘房内，二人见过，赵姨娘命小丫头倒了茶来与他吃。马道婆因见炕上堆着些零碎绸缎湾角，赵姨娘正粘鞋呢。马道婆道：“可是我正没了鞋面子了。赵奶奶你有零碎缎子，不拘什么颜色的，弄一双鞋面给我。”赵姨娘听说，便叹口气说道：“你瞧瞧那里头，还有那一块是成样的？成了样的东西，也不能到我手里来！有的没的都在这里，你不嫌，就挑两块子去。”马道婆见说，果真便挑了两块袖将起来。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Presently she reached Aunt Zhao’s room. After their greetings, Aunt Zhao told a little maid to pour her some tea. Mother Ma noticed a heap of odd scraps and offcuts of silk and satin on the kang, where Aunt Zhao was pasting shoes together.
‘Just when I’ve run out of material for shoe uppers!’ she said. ‘If you have any bits of satin, Mrs Zhao, whatever the colour, do let me have enough for a pair.’
‘Look through it yourself,’ Aunt Zhao sighed. ‘Is there a single decent piece there? Anything decent never reaches my hands. That’s all there is, good or bad. If you don’t mind it, choose a couple of pieces.’
Mother Ma duly chose two pieces and tucked them into her sleeve.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 却说林黛玉因见宝玉近日烫了脸，总不出门，倒时常在一处说说话儿。这日饭后看了两篇书，自觉无趣，便同紫鹃雪雁做了一回针线，更觉烦闷。便倚着房门出了一回神，信步出来，看阶下新迸出的稚笋，不觉出了院门。一望园中，四顾无人，惟见花光柳影，鸟语溪声。林黛玉信步便往怡红院中来，只见几个丫头舀水，都在回廊上围着看画眉洗澡呢。听见房内有笑声，林黛玉便入房中看时，原来是李宫裁、凤姐、宝钗都在这里呢，一见他进来都笑道：“这不又来了一个。”林黛玉笑道：“今儿齐全，谁下帖子请来的？”凤姐道：“前儿我打发了丫头送了两瓶茶叶去，你往那去了？”林黛玉笑道：“哦，可是倒忘了，多谢多谢。”凤姐儿又道：“你尝了可还好不好？”没有说完，宝玉便说道：“论理可倒罢了，只是我说不大甚好，也不知别人尝着怎么样。”宝钗道：“味倒轻，只是颜色不大好些。”凤姐道：“那是暹罗进贡来的。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Since Bao-yu had burnt his face and stopped going out, Dai-yu had often been able to sit and talk with him. One day, after a meal, she read a couple of passages, but found no pleasure in them. She did some needlework with Nightingale and Snowgoose, but that only made her more restless. After leaning in the doorway for a while in thought, she wandered out to look at the tender bamboo shoots newly thrusting up below the steps, and before she knew it had passed through the courtyard gate. In the garden she could see no one in any direction: only the brightness of flowers and the shadows of willows, with birds calling and water murmuring in the stream.
She strolled towards the House of Green Delights. Several maids were dipping up water and clustering in the covered walk to watch a thrush take its bath. Hearing laughter indoors, she went in and found Li Gong-cai, Xi-feng and Bao-chai all there.
‘Here’s another one!’ they said, laughing as she entered.
‘Everyone’s here today,’ Dai-yu said with a smile. ‘Who sent out the invitations?’
‘Where were you the other day when I sent a maid with two jars of tea for you?’ asked Xi-feng.
‘Oh, of course! I quite forgot. Thank you, thank you.’
‘Have you tried it? Did you like it?’
Before Xi-feng had finished, Bao-yu put in:
‘It ought to be all right, but I didn’t think much of it myself. I don’t know how the others found it.’
‘The flavour’s light,’ said Bao-chai, ‘but the colour isn’t very good.’
‘It came as tribute from Siam,’ said Xi-feng.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 凤姐笑道：“你别作梦！你给我们家作了媳妇，少什么？”指宝玉道：“你瞧瞧，人物儿、门第配不上，根基配不上，家私配不上？那一点还玷辱了谁呢？”林黛玉抬身就走。宝钗便叫：“颦儿急了，还不回来坐着。走了倒没意思。”说着便站起来拉住。刚至房门前，只见赵姨娘和周姨娘两个人进来瞧宝玉。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
‘Don’t be absurd!’ Xi-feng said, laughing. ‘What would you lack if you married into our family?’
She pointed to Bao-yu.
‘Look at him. Are his looks beneath you? His family? His standing? His wealth? Where’s the disgrace to anyone?’
Dai-yu rose to leave.
‘Little Pin-pin’s cross!’ Bao-chai called. ‘Come back and sit down. Going away will spoil it all.’
She rose to catch hold of her. They had just reached the doorway when Aunt Zhao and Aunt Zhou came in to see Bao-yu.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 这里宝玉拉着林黛玉的袖子，只是嘻嘻的笑，心里有话，只是口里说不出来。此时林黛玉只是禁不住把脸红涨了，挣着要走。宝玉忽然“嗳哟”了一声，说：“好头疼！”林黛玉道：“该，阿弥陀佛！”只见宝玉大叫一声：“我要死！”将身一纵，离地跳有三四尺高，口内乱嚷乱叫，说起胡话来了。林黛玉并丫头们都唬慌了，忙去报知王夫人、贾母等。此时王子腾的夫人也在这里，都一齐来时，宝玉益发拿刀弄杖，寻死觅活的，闹得天翻地覆。贾母、王夫人见了，唬的抖衣而颤，且“儿”一声“肉”一声放声恸哭。于是惊动诸人，连贾赦、邢夫人、贾珍、贾政、贾琏、贾蓉、贾芸、贾萍、薛姨妈、薛蟠并周瑞家的一干家中上上下下里里外外众媳妇丫头等，都来园内看视。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Bao-yu took hold of Dai-yu’s sleeve and could do nothing but grin. There was something in his heart, but he could not get it out. Dai-yu’s face grew redder in spite of herself, and she struggled to leave.
Suddenly Bao-yu gave a cry.
‘Oh, my head! What a pain!’
‘Serves you right. Amitabha!’ said Dai-yu.
‘I’m dying!’ he shouted.
He sprang three or four chi off the ground and began yelling and raving wildly. Dai-yu and the maids were terrified, and hurried to tell Lady Wang, Grandmother Jia and the others. Wang Zi-teng’s wife was there too. By the time they all arrived together, Bao-yu was brandishing knives and sticks, threatening to kill himself and throwing everything into turmoil. Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang shook so violently that their clothes trembled. Crying ‘My child!’ and ‘My own flesh!’, they broke into loud sobs.
The whole household was alarmed. Jia She, Lady Xing, Jia Zhen, Jia Zheng, Jia Lian, Jia Rong, Jia Yun, Jia Ping, Aunt Xue and Xue Pan, together with Zhou Rui’s wife and all the other married women-servants and maids, high and low, from the inner and outer quarters, came into the garden to see what was wrong.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 接着小史侯家、邢夫人弟兄辈并各亲戚眷属都来瞧看，也有送符水的，也有荐僧道的，总不见效。他叔嫂二人愈发糊涂，不省人事，睡在床上，浑身火炭一般，口内无般不说。到夜晚间，那些婆娘媳妇丫头们都不敢上前。因此把他二人都抬到王夫人的上房内，夜间派了贾芸带着小厮们挨次轮班看守。贾母、王夫人、邢夫人、薛姨妈等寸地不离，只围着干哭。
earlier_text_evidence.english: Then came people from the young Marquis Shi’s household, Lady Xing’s brothers and all the other relations. Some brought talisman water, others recommended monks and Taoists, but nothing did any good. Bao-yu and his cousin’s wife grew steadily more confused and lost all awareness of their surroundings. They lay in bed, their bodies hot as live coals, saying every kind of wild thing. By night the older women, the married servants and the maids dared not go near them. Both were therefore carried into Lady Wang’s principal apartments, and Jia Yun was put in charge of the pages who took turns keeping watch at night. Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, Lady Xing, Aunt Xue and the others would not move an inch away, but sat round them weeping helplessly.

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 一足高来一足低，
earlier_text_evidence.english: One foot rose high, the other dragged below,

earlier_text_evidence.chinese: 贾政一举目，见宝玉站在跟前，神彩飘逸，秀色夺人，看看贾环，人物委琐，举止荒疏，忽又想起贾珠来，再看看王夫人只有这一个亲生的儿子，素爱如珍，自己的胡须将已苍白：因这几件上，把素日嫌恶处分宝玉之心不觉减了八九。半晌说道：“娘娘吩咐说，你日日外头嬉游，渐次疏懒，如今叫禁管，同你姊妹在园里读书写字。你可好生用心习学，再如不守分安常，你可仔细！”宝玉连连的答应了几个“是”。王夫人便拉他在身旁坐下。他姊弟三人依旧坐下。
earlier_text_evidence.english:
Jia Zheng looked up. Before him stood Bao-yu, graceful and radiant, his beauty arresting. He glanced at Jia Huan, with his mean appearance and slovenly manners, and suddenly thought of Jia Zhu. Then he looked again at Lady Wang. This was the only son of her own she had left, and she had always cherished him like a treasure. His own beard was already turning grey. These thoughts together melted away eight or nine tenths of his usual dislike of Bao-yu and wish to punish him. After a long pause he said:
‘Her Highness says you spend your days running about outside and are growing ever more idle. You are now to be kept under supervision, studying and practising your writing in the garden with your sisters. Apply yourself properly. If you fail again to behave as you should, you had better look out!’
Bao-yu answered, ‘Yes, sir,’ several times in quick succession. Lady Wang drew him down to sit beside her. The other three sat down again.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 正说着，只见一个小丫头掀帘跑进来，喘着气道：「太太，老太太那边打发鹦鹉姐姐来请，请太太即刻就过去呢。」王夫人听了，忙起身更衣，命玉钏儿看屋子。临出门，回头看了宝玉一眼，方带着人一径往贾母院里去了。宝玉见几上汝窑美人觚空着，也没插花，便退了出来。
later_text_evidence.english: As they were speaking, a young maid lifted the curtain and ran in, out of breath.  ‘Your Ladyship, Her Old Ladyship has sent Parrot to ask you to come over at once.’  Lady Wang got up hurriedly to change, telling Silver to look after the room. At the door she turned to look at Bao-yu before setting off with her attendants straight for Grandmother Jia’s courtyard. Bao-yu noticed that the slender Ru-ware beauty vase on the table was empty, with no flowers in it, and withdrew.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 宝玉把屋里的人叫到一处，自己站着，倒像犯了什么错的一般，方说道：「太太那里已有话。谁家里来领，便由家里领去。佳蕙的姥姥家已经来接，秋纹家里也来问过两遭。」说着，眼圈先红了，又道：「我给你们银子。不是我要撵你们。」
later_text_evidence.english: Bao-yu called the maids together. He stood before them looking as though he had done something wrong.  ‘Mother has given her orders. Anyone whose family comes to fetch her is to go home with them. Melilot’s grandmother has already sent someone, and Ripple’s family have asked twice.’  His eyes reddened before he could go on.  ‘I’ll give you money. It isn’t I who want to send you away.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 秋纹便不问了，冷笑道：「怎么偏先轮到我？绮霰怎么不走？他来的还比我晚呢。」麝月轻轻唤了一声「秋纹姐姐」。秋纹不理，只把手里一件藕荷百蝶穿花洋缎褂子抖了又叠，叠了又抖，道：「那一年太太赏的衣裳，我还收着呢。」正说着，只见小红从外头进来，手里捧着一个秋香色羽缎小包袱，说是奉琏二奶奶之命送与二爷的，放下便去了。
later_text_evidence.english: Ripple asked no more. She gave a cold laugh.  ‘Why should it be my turn first? Why isn’t Mackerel going? She came here after I did.’  ‘Sister Ripple,’ Musk said softly.  Ripple paid no attention. She shook out and folded the jacket she held, then shook it out again: lilac foreign satin patterned with a hundred butterflies among flowers.  ‘I’ve still got the clothes Her Ladyship gave me that year.’  As she spoke, Crimson came in with a small parcel wrapped in olive-green camlet. She said Mrs Lian had sent it to Master Bao, put it down and left.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 秋纹看着他出了院门，笑道：「当日他不过替二爷倒了碗茶，我还啐过他，说他也不照照镜子。如今倒是他在那边好好的。」又向麝月道：「你留下自然是好的。」麝月不作声。秋纹自觉说重了，道：「我不是怪你。」褂子叠了又抖，总叠不成个齐整样儿。忽又道：「我出去了，谁早起给二爷梳头，谁记得二爷吃药的时辰。」麝月忙道：「有我呢。」秋纹回身整理架上的书，手却不动。
later_text_evidence.english: Ripple watched her go out through the courtyard gate.  ‘All she did that day was pour Master Bao a bowl of tea,’ she said, laughing. ‘And I spat at her, and told her she ought to take a look in the mirror. Now she’s over there, doing very well for herself.’  She turned to Musk.  ‘Of course it’s all right for you. You’re staying.’  Musk said nothing. Ripple felt she had spoken too harshly.  ‘I’m not blaming you.’  She folded the jacket and shook it out again, but could not get it into a neat shape. Suddenly she said:  ‘When I’m gone, who’s going to comb Master Bao’s hair in the morning? Who’s going to remember when it’s time for his medicine?’  ‘I’m here,’ Musk said quickly.  Ripple turned to straighten the books on the shelf, but her hands did not move.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 绮霰倚着门框站着，道：「我原是老太太拨过来的，就在这儿守着罢了。」说着，自去拿了块西洋印花软布，一样一样拭案上的笔筒砚台，再不多言。
later_text_evidence.english: Mackerel stood leaning against the door-frame.  ‘Her Old Ladyship sent me here in the first place. I shall just stay where I am.’  She fetched a piece of soft Western printed cloth and wiped the brush-pots and inkstones on the desk one by one, without another word.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 独有佳蕙，不哭也不闹，只默默收拾自己的东西：两件旧衣裳，一面小镜子，一个针线包，包在一块靛青土布里，打成一个四方小包，一只手便拎得起。他姥姥家的人已在外头等着，对牌亦销了名。收拾停当，提着包袱走到院门口，忽站住，回过头，望院里从前小红住过的西厢房看了一眼。屋门闭着，窗纸破了一块。看了那一眼，便转身出去了。
later_text_evidence.english: Melilot alone neither cried nor made a fuss, but silently gathered her things: two old garments, a little mirror and a sewing bag. She wrapped them in a piece of indigo homespun and tied it into a small square bundle that she could carry in one hand. Someone from her grandmother’s household was already waiting outside, and her name had been struck off the tally register. When everything was ready, she picked up her bundle and walked to the courtyard gate. There she suddenly stopped, turned her head and looked once at the west-side room where Crimson used to live. The door was shut, and there was a tear in the window-paper. After that one look she turned and went out.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 正闷着，可巧茗烟悄悄进来回道：「锦香院的云姑娘打发人来，说有要紧的话，定要当面回二爷才罢。」宝玉遂托言往城外庙里还愿，只带了茗烟出门。原来是一座小庙，香火冷落。风过处，殿角的铁马丁零丁零响了一阵。云儿已在庙前等着，见了礼，同到廊下坐了。
later_text_evidence.english: While he sat fretting, Tealeaf happened to slip in with a message.  ‘Miss Nuageuse at the Budding Grove has sent someone to say she has something important to tell you. She insists on speaking to you herself, Master Bao.’  Bao-yu made the excuse that he was going to fulfil a vow at a temple outside the city, and went out with Tealeaf alone. It was a small temple with few worshippers. A gust of wind set the iron chimes at the corners of the hall tinkling for a while. Nuageuse was waiting in front of the temple. After they had exchanged greetings, they went to sit under the verandah.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 云儿笑道：「太太总不至于亏了他。若说妥当人家，我倒想起一个。琪官这几年在城东置了田地房舍，一个人过着，至今也没娶。那年在冯大爷家，他念了一句『花气袭人』，还是我替他说破的。」
later_text_evidence.english: ‘Surely Her Ladyship wouldn’t treat her badly,’ Nuageuse said with a smile. ‘As for a suitable household, I can think of one. Bijou has bought land and a house east of the city these last few years. He lives alone, and he’s still unmarried. You remember that time at Mr Feng’s, when he recited “The flowers’ aroma steals upon us”? I was the one who pointed it out.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 宝玉笑道：「你的事我应了。我那里有一只金西洋自行船，还有一只金麒麟，你先拿去使。琪官那头我另有个凭据，一并叫茗烟送与你。」
later_text_evidence.english: ‘I’ll help you with your business,’ said Bao-yu, smiling. ‘I have a Western gold mechanical boat, and a gold qilin too. You can have those to use for now. And I have a token to send to Bijou. I’ll send it all to you by Tealeaf.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 宝玉回来，开了箱子，翻寻出一条大红汗巾来，看了一回，又取下十锦格子上的金西洋自行船，连旧荷包里的金麒麟，用旧绢包了，一并交与茗烟，附耳吩咐了几句。茗烟会意，悄悄去了。
later_text_evidence.english: When Bao-yu got home, he opened his chest and searched out a scarlet sash. He looked at it for a while, then took the Western gold mechanical boat down from the curio shelves and the gold qilin from an old purse. He wrapped them in old silk, handed everything to Tealeaf and whispered a few instructions in his ear. Tealeaf understood and slipped away.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 过了七八日，茗烟回来回道：「蒋大爷一口应承，只说这是几生修来的福分。日子已拣定了，二月十二花朝。」宝玉听了，怔了一怔，只说：「知道了。」云儿亦叫茗烟捎话来，说那只船他不敢自专，已托蒋玉菡在外头寻个买主。
later_text_evidence.english: Seven or eight days later Tealeaf came back with his report.  ‘Mr Jiang agreed at once. He said it was a blessing he must have earned over several lifetimes. The date’s settled: the twelfth of the second month, the Festival of Flowers.’  Bao-yu was taken aback for a moment when he heard this.  ‘I see,’ was all he said.  Nuageuse had also sent word through Tealeaf that she had not felt she ought to dispose of the boat on her own, and had asked Jiang Yu-han to find a buyer for it outside.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 袭人不答这话，只说：「你我从小在一处的，这些年走的人也不少了。媚人姐姐也是这个时节嫁的，嫁的是外头一户平常人家，此后就没信儿了。茜雪去了那些年，也不知在那里。小红倒跟了琏二奶奶去，如今还在那边。」又低声道：「可人呢。先时二爷屋里丢了一件东西，那一夜是他当的值，问了两遭，第二日人就没了。后来良儿的事发出来，谁又替他说过一句。他和金钏儿，如今是一处了。」
later_text_evidence.english: Aroma did not answer the question.  ‘You and I have been together since we were children,’ she said. ‘A good many have gone these last few years. Winsome was married at this time of year too, to an ordinary family outside. We never heard from her again. Snowpink’s been gone for years, and I don’t know where she is. Crimson, at least, went to Mrs Lian and is still there.’  She lowered her voice.  ‘And Charmer? Something went missing from Master Bao’s rooms once. She’d been on duty that night. They questioned her twice, and next day she was gone. When the business about Honesty came out afterwards, who said a word for her? She and Golden are in the same place now.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 这一日掌灯时分，紫绡过来帮着收衣裳。灯芯结了花。箱笼半开，叠好的衣裳齐齐压在一边，其余几件还搭在炕沿，二人一个递，一个收。一时收完了，袭人在灯下坐着，手里一只旧黄花梨细雕小匣，巴掌大小；匣面刻着梅花一枝，刻痕极浅，几乎磨平了。袭人将匣子推过去，道：「这是你的，打开瞧瞧。」
later_text_evidence.english: One evening, at lamplighting time, Purple Silk came to help put away the clothes. A flower of soot had formed on the lamp-wick. The chests stood half open, the folded clothes neatly pressed down on one side, while a few remaining pieces hung over the edge of the kang. One girl passed them over and the other packed them. When they had finished, Aroma sat under the lamp holding a small, finely carved box of old huanghuali wood, no bigger than her palm. A spray of plum blossom was carved on the lid, so shallowly that the lines had almost worn away. Aroma pushed it across.  ‘This is yours. Open it and see.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 袭人忙伸手按住匣子，笑道：「你只管拿着。你这一份，我早替你收下了。檀云的一份也还在我这里，他走的时候不曾带去。」说着又道：「你别怕。二爷不会赶你，家里若来接，他也不会强留你。往后你若回父母家，别叫人哄了去；若还在这里，听麝月姐姐的话。将来配人，也要求人打听清楚。」
later_text_evidence.english: Aroma put out a hand to hold the box where it was and smiled.  ‘Take it. I put your share aside long ago. I’ve still got Sandal’s share too. She didn’t take it when she went.’  Then she added:  ‘Don’t be afraid. Master Bao won’t turn you out, and if your family comes for you, he won’t force you to stay. If you go home to your parents one day, don’t let anyone cheat you. If you stay here, listen to Musk. And when there’s talk of a husband for you, ask someone to make proper inquiries.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 紫绡听了，便悄悄的问：「檀云姐姐出去，后来可有信儿？」袭人不答，只伸手轻轻合上匣盖，方收回手去。紫绡见他不答，便不好再问，抱着匣子站起来，低声道：「姐姐出门子那日，我一定一早起来送。」袭人点头。
later_text_evidence.english: Purple Silk asked quietly:  ‘Has there ever been any news of Sandal since she left?’  Aroma did not answer. She only reached out and gently closed the lid of the box, then drew back her hand. Seeing that she would not answer, Purple Silk could not very well ask again. She stood up with the box in her arms.  ‘On your wedding day I’ll be up early to see you off,’ she said softly.  Aroma nodded.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 至晚客散，房里只剩他两个。桌角上搁着新添的几副粗瓷碗箸，红纸还未拆尽；银盆尚裹着棉布，倚在墙边。窗纸新糊，灯影照处，尚见几道浆痕。蒋玉菡自怀里取出一件东西，摊在灯下，是一条大红汗巾子，笑道：「二爷是拿这个来说合的。这原是我的东西，那一年在冯大爷家里，我系了送给二爷的。没想到转了这几年，倒又回来了。」
later_text_evidence.english: That evening, when the guests had gone, the two of them were alone in their room. The newly added sets of coarse porcelain bowls and chopsticks stood at one corner of the table, with some of their red-paper wrappings still on. The silver basins, still wrapped in cotton cloth, rested against the wall. The windows had been newly papered, and in the lamplight a few streaks of paste could still be seen. Jiang Yu-han took something from inside his robe and spread it under the lamp. It was a scarlet sash.  ‘This is what Master Bao used to make the match,’ he said, smiling. ‘It was mine to begin with. I was wearing it that day at Mr Feng’s, when I gave it to him. Who would have thought it would come back after all these years?’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 袭人看着汗巾，伸手拿起来翻过一面看了看，隔了这几年，尚有一缕香气，又搁下。正看着，忽见蒋玉菡腰里露出一截带子来，是松花绿的，颜色洗得极淡了。袭人指着道：「你这条，是那里来的？」蒋玉菡道：「也是那一日二爷解下来给我的，我系了这几年了。」
later_text_evidence.english: Aroma looked at the sash, picked it up and turned it over. Even after these years a trace of fragrance remained. She set it down again. As she looked, she noticed the end of a sash showing at Jiang Yu-han’s waist. It was pine-pollen green, washed almost colourless. She pointed to it.  ‘Where did that one come from?’  ‘Master Bao took it off and gave it to me that same day,’ said Jiang Yu-han. ‘I’ve been wearing it all these years.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 蒋玉菡怔了，抬头看他。袭人道：「当日二爷拿了去给人，我还问他要过。他说赔我一条，到底也没赔。」
later_text_evidence.english: Jiang Yu-han was taken aback and looked up at her.  ‘When Master Bao gave it away that day, I asked him for it back,’ said Aroma. ‘He said he would give me another one. He never did.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 蒋玉菡把腰里那条也解下来，同大红的并排搁在灯下，一红一绿。袭人看了一会子，忽笑了一声，道：「这么着说来，倒是这两条带子先做了亲，咱们倒在后头。」蒋玉菡也笑道：「这话倒新鲜。」便一并收进一个小箱子里锁了。
later_text_evidence.english: Jiang Yu-han untied the sash from his waist and laid it beside the scarlet one under the lamp, one red, one green. Aroma looked at them for a while, then suddenly laughed.  ‘So these two sashes were married before we were. We’ve come afterwards.’  ‘That’s a new way of putting it,’ Jiang Yu-han said, laughing too.  He put them both in a little chest and locked it.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 宝玉不作声，遂伸手端起那半盏梨汤，已是凉的，因向紫鹃道：「这个凉了，快换热的来。」紫鹃答应一声，端了下去。宝玉只见案上放着一卷书，便伸手拿过来看，却是一卷《庄子》。
later_text_evidence.english: Bao-yu said nothing. He reached for the half-cup of pear broth and found it cold. ‘This has gone cold,’ he told Nightingale. ‘Do bring some hot.’ Nightingale assented and took it away. Noticing a book on the table, he picked it up. It was a volume of Zhuang-zi.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 却说上头议宝玉亲事，虽是议而不决，谁知风声早传到了下头。园里几个婆子，趁没差使，凑在沁芳亭背风的粉壁下歇脚，这个剥菱角米，那个纳鞋底，一面东家长西家短的说些闲话。剥下的菱角壳堆在脚边；纳鞋底的婆子拿针在鬓边蹭了两下，麻线勒得指头上一道道白印。说着说着，便说到宝玉的亲事上头。剥菱角米的婆子把壳往脚边一拨，笑道：「前儿上房收拾屋子，只怕二爷的事近了。」纳鞋底的把鞋底翻了个面，接口道：「谁说不是。我们那边领月钱，还听见问年庚呢。」又一个道：「阿弥陀佛，我倒听见说老爷心里另有个人，说是可怜他没爹没娘的。是谁我可不敢混说。」你一言我一语，竟说出三四个样子来。这一个道：「依我看，还是林姑娘。前年姨太太在潇湘馆亲口说，要把林姑娘说给二爷，当着一屋子人说的。」那一个道：「你知道什么。姨太太是说顽话。我听见说，薛家要搬进来办亲呢。」又一个道：「都是混说。两家都还没定，不过拿这话拘着二爷念书罢了。」又一个道：「读书？依我说，这府里如今真念书的，只剩稻香村兰哥儿一个，天不亮就听见书声了。」这一个道：「可不是。四姑娘倒好，成日只描他那张园子图，画了一年多，听说才画到半张。」
later_text_evidence.english: Meanwhile, although the elders had come to no decision about Bao-yu's marriage, word of their discussions had already reached the servants. A few of the older women, with no errand to run, had gathered to rest beside the whitewashed wall on the sheltered side of Drenched Blossoms Pavilion. One was shelling water-caltrops, another stitching shoe-soles, and they chatted about this household and that. Empty shells piled up at their feet. The woman stitching soles rubbed her needle against the hair at her temple; the hemp thread left white grooves across her fingers. Presently the talk turned to Bao-yu's marriage. Pushing some shells aside with her hand, the first woman laughed. ‘They were putting the mistress's rooms to rights the other day. I dare say Master Bao's turn is coming.’ The woman with the shoe-sole turned it over. ‘Indeed it is. When we went to collect our monthly money, I heard them asking about birth dates.’ Another put in, ‘Bless the Buddha, I heard the master has someone else in mind. Says he pities her for having neither father nor mother. But I wouldn't venture to say who.’ Between them they produced three or four different versions. ‘If you ask me,’ said one, ‘it will be Miss Lin. The year before last, at the Naiad's House, Aunt Xue said with her own lips that she would make a match between Miss Lin and Master Bao. Said it before a whole roomful of people.’ ‘What do you know? Aunt Xue was joking. I heard the Xues are moving in to arrange the wedding.’ ‘Nonsense, all of it,’ said another. ‘Neither family has settled anything. They're only using it to keep Master Bao at his books.’ ‘Books? If you ask me, the only one left in this household who really studies is young Master Lan at Sweet-rice Village. You can hear him reading before daylight.’ ‘True enough. Miss Xi-chun has the best of it, painting that picture of the garden all day long. She's been at it more than a year, and they say she's only halfway through.’

later_text_evidence.chinese: 少时王太医来了，诊了左手又诊右手，在床前坐了半天，方起身出去。贾政·贾琏紧跟至外间动问。王太医悄悄的说道：「外感已退，非药石所能攻。如今心气已衰，胃气又弱，只宜静养，顺着老人家的性情罢，只有定数了。」贾政听了，叹道：「也只好尽人事罢了。」贾琏转身回来，勉强陪笑道：「老太太放心，太医说不过秋燥伤了些，等天气清凉，自然就好了。」贾母看着他道：「你不用虚宽我的心。我活了这些年，自己身上还不知道么。只怕熬不过今年了。」贾琏不敢接这话，只低了头。房里一时只闻药炉水滚，鸳鸯拿火箸拨开了炭，鹦鹉端了痰盒出去倒，琥珀掖好帐角，谁也不敢则声。
later_text_evidence.english: Presently Doctor Wang arrived. He felt the pulse at her left wrist, then at her right, and sat a long time beside the bed before rising and going out. Jia Zheng and Jia Lian followed him into the outer room to ask his opinion. Doctor Wang spoke very quietly. “The external disorder has subsided; this is not something medicines can remedy. The heart's vital energy is now failing, and the stomach's is weak. All she should have is quiet rest. Let the old lady have her own way. The rest is ordained.” Jia Zheng sighed. “We can only do what lies in our power.” Jia Lian went back in and forced a smile. “Don't worry, Grandmother. The doctor says it is only a little harm done by the autumn dryness. Once the weather turns cool, you will get better of yourself.” Grandmother Jia looked at him. “You needn't give me false comfort. I have lived all these years; do you think I don't know my own body? I am afraid I shan't last the year.” Jia Lian dared not answer this, but only lowered his head. For a while the only sound in the room was the water boiling on the medicine stove. Faithful parted the charcoal with the fire-tongs; Parrot carried out the spittoon to empty it; Amber tucked in the corner of the bed-curtain. No one dared make a sound.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 一行人过了沁芳亭。往年这时节，桂花香透几重院落，廊下摆满了菊花；如今园中花木少人收拾，沟边枯叶成堆，扫之不尽；几架蔷薇只剩空藤，风一过便沙沙作响。稻香村外，稻穗倒伏；藕香榭下，残荷欹斜，水面浮着几片碎萍。贾母一路看着，到了藕香榭方命停下。众人早备下两席清淡酒果，不过菊花酒·糕饼果碟几样。贾母看了一看席上，笑道：「往年这时候，这里早摆上螃蟹了罢。」鸳鸯忙陪笑道：「老太太自己说的，那东西虽好吃，不是什么好的。」贾母也笑了，道：「倒拿我的话来堵我。」贾母只叫女孩儿们坐近些，又笑道：「水边还有几尾鱼，你们何不钓上来，取个乐儿。」婆子们便送上几根短竿来。宝玉抢先拿了一根，见浮子才动，忙往上一提，那钩子却挂住了石缝，钓竿往青石上一磕，「拍」的一声，折成两段，连钩子亦不知那里去了。
later_text_evidence.english: The party passed the Drenched Blossoms Pavilion. In former years, at this season, the fragrance of the osmanthus had filled courtyard after courtyard, and the verandahs had been lined with chrysanthemums. Now there were few to tend the garden's flowers and trees. Dead leaves lay in heaps beside the channels, and there was no sweeping them all away. Several rose trellises held nothing but bare vines, which rustled whenever the wind blew. Outside Sweet-rice Village the ears of rice lay flattened; below the Lotus Pavilion the withered lotus stalks leaned awry, and a few broken patches of duckweed floated on the water. Grandmother Jia looked about her all the way, and only on reaching the Lotus Pavilion did she order them to stop. Two tables had already been laid with light refreshments: chrysanthemum wine, cakes and pastries, and a few dishes of fruit. Grandmother Jia glanced at the tables and smiled. “In other years, at this time, there would have been crabs laid out here already, wouldn't there?” Faithful hastened to smile back. “Your Old Ladyship said yourself that, tasty as they are, they are not good for one.” Grandmother Jia laughed too. “So you are stopping my mouth with my own words.” She simply had the girls sit closer to her, and went on smiling. “There are still a few fish by the bank. Why don't you catch some, to amuse yourselves?” The old women brought over several short rods. Bao-yu was the first to seize one. No sooner had the float stirred than he jerked it up, but the hook had caught in a crevice between the stones. The rod struck a blue flagstone and snapped in two with a crack; even the hook vanished no one knew where.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 重阳后又过了几日，贾母的精神又减了几分。这日晚间，便叫鸳鸯并旁人都出去歇歇，单留下琥珀一个在跟前。琥珀坐在脚踏边，替他轻轻捶腿。贾母忽问：「你跟了我几年了？」琥珀道：「回老太太，七年了。」贾母道：「七年，也不短了。你是个静孩子，我有一句话，只托你传。」琥珀忙跪下道：「老太太吩咐。」贾母望着帐顶，半日方说道：「敏儿小时候，比林丫头还爱哭。他出阁那日，进轿前还回来抱了我一回。后来病没了，我连他末后一面也不曾见着。」说到这里住了口，方悄悄的道：「我的女儿没了。他的女儿就是我的心肝儿肉。命根子总要跟心肝儿肉在一处。」琥珀伏地听着。贾母又道：「等我闭了眼，把这句话告诉老爷。只这一句，别添别减。」琥珀道：「是。」贾母闭上眼，再不言语。琥珀又坐回脚踏，见贾母的手露在被外，便轻轻放进被里去。
later_text_evidence.english: A few days after the Double Ninth, Grandmother Jia's strength declined still further. One evening she told Faithful and the others to go out and rest, keeping only Amber beside her. Amber sat by the footstool, gently patting her legs. Suddenly Grandmother Jia asked, “How many years have you been with me?” “Seven years, Your Old Ladyship,” Amber replied. “Seven years. That is no short time. You are a quiet child. There is something I want said, and I entrust it to you alone.” Amber knelt at once. “Your Old Ladyship has only to command me.” Grandmother Jia looked up at the canopy, and only after a long while said, “When Min was little, she cried even more readily than our little Lin. On her wedding day, before getting into the bridal chair, she came back and hugged me once more. Later she fell ill and died, and I never even saw her one last time.” She broke off, then said very softly, “My daughter is gone. Her daughter is my heart's own flesh. The one who is my very life must always be with my heart's own flesh.” Amber listened with her face to the ground. Grandmother Jia went on, “When I have closed my eyes, tell the Master those words. Just those words: add nothing and leave nothing out.” “Yes,” said Amber. Grandmother Jia closed her eyes and spoke no more. Amber sat down again by the footstool. Seeing Grandmother Jia's hand lying outside the quilt, she gently put it back beneath the covers.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 又过了一日，贾母自觉精神短了，便命贾政王夫人·邢夫人·李纨凤姐等都到跟前，宝玉姊妹们也在帘外候着。先叫翡翠到湘云跟前，道：「你随云丫头去，和翠缕作个伴。他性子爽，细处未必顾得到，你替我照应些。」湘云忙跪下道：「老祖宗身边少不得人，我不要。」贾母笑道：「我这里还少人么。你只管领去就是了。」又叫珍珠·玻璃到宝琴跟前，道：「琴儿往后若再跟船往南边去，你两个随他。船上日子不比家里，凡事仔细些。」宝琴含泪答应了。贾母方望着贾政·王夫人，明嘱道：「宝玉的大事，要趁早些办了，不必等我。我若有个好歹，也不许你们拘着服制，误了他的正经事。」众人都垂手听着。贾政躬身应是。
later_text_evidence.english: Another day passed. Feeling her strength grow short, Grandmother Jia ordered Jia Zheng, Lady Wang, Lady Xing, Li Wan, Xi-feng and the others to come to her bedside. Bao-yu and the girls waited outside the curtain too. First she called Jade over to Xiang-yun. “You are to go with our little Yun and be a companion to Kingfisher. Our Yun has an open, easy nature and may not think of the little things. See to them for her on my behalf.” Xiang-yun knelt at once. “Grandmother, you cannot spare anyone from your side. I don't want her.” Grandmother Jia smiled. “Am I short of people here? Just take her with you.” Then she called Pearl and Glass over to Bao-qin. “If Qin goes south by boat again, you two are to go with her. Life on a boat is not like life at home. Take care over everything.” Bao-qin answered through her tears. Grandmother Jia now looked at Jia Zheng and Lady Wang and gave her instructions plainly. “Bao-yu's marriage must be arranged soon. There is no need to wait for me. If anything should happen to me, you must not let the mourning observances hold you back and delay this important business of his.” They all listened with their hands respectfully lowered. Jia Zheng bowed and assented.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 到底贾政发了话，命贾琏把府中值钱的东西开个单子，该当的当，该卖的卖。贾琏同林之孝查了两日，单上开的皆是碧玺猫儿眼·汝窑玉壶春这些旧年的体面物件。及至开库，只见几件古玩剩了空匣，盘问底下人，人人都说不知。恒舒典来人垂手回道：「朝奉说，近来府里下人拿簪环器皿去当的络绎不绝，店里压了许多死货，实在拿不出大钱来收。」贾政无法，乃将家中所藏唐寅·董其昌几轴书画，托了熟人，卖与城中富户；车马·桌几里头值钱的，亦叫林之孝拉到菜市口摆开卖了。早起标一个价，晌午便让一成，到日头偏西，竟半价与了人。看的人多，买的人少。林之孝回来回道：「买家把价压得死，半分也不肯再添。」贾政问卖了多少，他便报了个数来，贾政拿笔在单上记了。
later_text_evidence.english: In the end Jia Zheng spoke, ordering Jia Lian to draw up a list of the mansion's valuables: what could be pawned must be pawned, and what could be sold must be sold. Jia Lian and Lin Zhi-xiao spent two days making an inventory. Their list was full of the treasures that had lent the household distinction in years past: tourmalines, cat's-eyes and pear-shaped Ru-ware vases. But when the storerooms were opened, several of the antiques had left only empty boxes behind. The servants were questioned, and every one professed ignorance. A man from Heng-shu's pawnshop stood with his hands respectfully lowered and reported, “The appraiser says that lately there has been a constant stream of your servants bringing in hairpins, bracelets, vessels and utensils to pawn. The shop has a great deal of unsaleable stock on its hands, and really cannot find any large sum to take more.” Having no other course, Jia Zheng entrusted several scrolls of painting and calligraphy by Tang Yin and Dong Qichang from the family collection to an acquaintance, who sold them to wealthy households in the city. Such carriages, horses, tables and stands as were worth anything were also taken by Lin Zhi-xiao to the Vegetable Market crossroads and put up for sale. A price would be marked in the morning and reduced by a tenth at noon; by late afternoon the things were being let go for half-price. There were many lookers and few buyers. When Lin Zhi-xiao returned, he reported, “The buyers drove the price down to the very bottom. They would not add the smallest fraction.” Jia Zheng asked how much the sale had brought. He named a figure, and Jia Zheng took up his brush and entered it on the list.

later_text_evidence.chinese: 满屋的人都唬呆了。邢夫人脸上一阵红，一阵白，想要说话，却被这一通骂堵得说不出。凤姐坐在外间，听得字字分明，手扶着桌沿勉强站了起来。鸳鸯并不停，又骂：
later_text_evidence.english: Everyone in the room was stunned. Lady Xing turned red, then white. She wanted to speak, but the torrent of abuse left her unable to get a word out. Xi-feng, sitting in the outer room, heard every word distinctly. With a hand on the edge of the table, she struggled to her feet. Faithful did not stop, but went on cursing:

later_text_evidence.chinese: 周瑞家的回道：「回太太，四姑娘终日闭门，连饭也是彩屏在门口接进去的。妙玉姑娘也少出来。」
later_text_evidence.english: “Yes, Your Ladyship,” Zhou Rui's wife replied. “The Fourth Miss keeps her door shut all day. Even her meals are handed to Cai-ping at the door and taken in. Miss Adamantina seldom comes out either.”

later_text_evidence.chinese: 又拿出一串小钥匙交给翠墨，道：「我屋里留下的东西，姑娘们看着分。姨娘每月那几两，照旧领，不必因我去了就减。」
later_text_evidence.english: She also took out a ring of small keys and handed it to Ebony. “Let the young ladies divide up whatever I leave in my rooms, as they think best. Aunt Zhao is to draw her few taels each month as usual. They need not be reduced because I have gone.”

later_text_evidence.chinese: 翠墨接了钥匙，道：「姑娘不用再嘱咐。」
later_text_evidence.english: Ebony took the keys. “You needn't remind me again, miss.”

later_text_evidence.chinese: 到了渡口，只见官船泊在江心，岸边另有小舟接送。有个撑船的隔水喊道：「府里的，这边来！」说着把小舟撑近石岸。王府仪从并不甚多，旗幡都叫风卷着。江风正紧，浪头一个赶着一个，扑在岸石上，碎作一层白沫。贾政·王夫人·李纨·宝玉·宝钗等送到岸上。赵姨娘竟没来，只叫翠墨送了个喜鹊登梅妆缎香袋。翠墨将香袋交与探春，道：「姨娘那边有我。」
later_text_evidence.english: At the landing they saw the official ship moored in midstream, with a small boat by the bank to ferry passengers out. A boatman called across the water, “You from the mansion! This way!” and poled his boat towards the stone bank. The Prince's ceremonial escort was not very large. The wind twisted its flags and pennants. A strong wind was blowing down the river, and wave pursued wave, flinging themselves against the stones and breaking into white foam. Jia Zheng, Lady Wang, Li Wan, Bao-yu, Bao-chai and the others came down to the bank to see her off. Aunt Zhao did not come at all; she merely sent Ebony with a scented sachet of figured satin, showing a magpie perched on plum blossom. As Ebony handed it to Tan-chun, she said, “I'll be there for Aunt Zhao.”

later_text_evidence.chinese: 探春船去之次日，西宁王府先遣长史往宁国府传话，说要认四姑娘为义女，择日接入王府。贾珍当下便应了。次后王府一纸公文才送到荣府，王夫人因叫人往惜春院中传话。那婆子到了院门，只见彩屏坐在门外，脚边放着一盆冷水。
later_text_evidence.english: The day after Tan-chun's ship left, the Prince of Xining's household first sent its chief secretary to the Ning mansion with word that the Prince wished to adopt the Fourth Miss as his daughter and choose a day to bring her into his household. Jia Zhen agreed at once. Only afterwards did a formal dispatch arrive at the Rong mansion. Lady Wang sent someone to Xi-chun's courtyard with the message. When the old woman reached the gate, she found Cai-ping sitting outside the door, a basin of cold water at her feet.
